steps.message:
Item 051 on the Package A verification register is assigned to me and falls due on 07/20/2026, two days before the Level-3 placement. It covers the Block C spread footings and the long-term settlement of the clay beneath them.

Work through Item 051 against the project record and issue the verification memo. Set out what you reviewed, the basis you applied, your findings with the working behind them, and the disposition. Where something has to be produced before the item can be closed, say what it is and who is required to produce it.

Use the attached memorandum form and keep its sections. Write it from Rahul Nimkar, Geotechnical Reviewer, to Adrian Vance, Project Engineer, copied to Rachel Marlbeck. Save it as Thelbridge_Verification_Memo_Item051_BlockC.docx.

1.  EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
Kelbrook Geotechnical, Inc. has completed a subsurface investigation and geotechnical engineering analysis for
Package A of the Birchwood Village Expansion Program at 1802 Larchwood Avenue, Columbus, Ohio.
Package A comprises three student-housing blocks (Blocks A, B and C) constructed over a shared podium, with
a single basement level beneath Blocks A and B, and a separate deep plant-room excavation planned beneath
Block B.
The finished design grade across Package A is established at El. 750.0 ft. Existing ground surface stands at
approximately El. 750.0 across the footprints of Blocks A and C but falls to about El. 738.0 across the Block B
footprint (a former surface drainage swale). Placement of engineered fill of variable thickness — up to
approximately 12 ft beneath Block B — will therefore be required to bring the site to design grade.
The subsurface profile consists of three principal strata:
•  Stratum 1 — Upper sand, classified SP-SM (poorly-graded sand with silt), medium-dense, from
existing grade down to El. 738.0, total unit weight 118 pcf.
•  Stratum 2 — Compressible clay aquitard, classified CL (lean clay of medium plasticity),
normally-consolidated, from El. 738.0 down to El. 720.0 (18 ft thick), total unit weight 120 pcf, low
permeability. This is the strata governing settlement of shallow foundations and provides the aquitard
between the shallow and deep groundwater regimes.
•  Stratum 3 — Dense sand and gravel aquifer, classified SW-GW, below El. 720.0, total unit weight 130
pcf, confined by the overlying clay.
Groundwater is present as two distinct regimes:
•  The design water table in the upper sand is set at El. 742.0 ft. Piezometer readings taken from three
shallow standpipes over the 11/2024–02/2025 monitoring period range from El. 741.6 to El. 742.4;
groundwater seepage was observed at El. 741.8 to El. 742.2 in the Block A test-pit excavation.
•  A confined piezometric head of El. 738.0 ft has been measured in the deep sand-and-gravel aquifer
through two deep piezometers screened below El. 720.0, with readings ranging El. 737.7 to El. 738.3. The
confined head is at essentially the same elevation as the top of the clay aquitard.
Consolidation testing on two undisturbed Shelby-tube samples of the compressible clay (samples B-06 U3 and
B-08 U2, tested per ASTM D2435) yielded a compression index Cc = 0.28, a recompression index Cr = 0.045,
an initial void ratio e0 = 0.92, an in-situ vertical effective stress σ'0 = 1,850 psf, and a preconsolidation pressure
σ'p = 1,900 psf. The margin (σ'p − σ'0 ≈ 50 psf) confirms the clay is essentially normally-consolidated: any net
stress increase applied at the top of the clay will produce virgin (Cc) compression rather than recompression
(Cr) compression.
Principal geotechnical recommendations are as follows:
1.  Block C — Spread footings may be founded within the upper sand. Consolidation of the underlying
compressible clay under column-load stress increases at mid-depth of the clay must be explicitly computed
by the Structural Engineer of Record, using the parameters provided herein, and reconciled against the
settlement tolerances specified in the project structural criteria.
2.  Blocks A and B basement mat — A conventional reinforced-concrete mat foundation may be founded
within the upper sand at the design underside elevation. Hydrostatic uplift from the El. 742.0 water table
must be resolved by mat self-weight, superimposed permanent loads and, where necessary, tension
elements. The waterproofing system for the below-grade envelope must be selected for the applicable

3.  SITE DESCRIPTION AND GEOLOGIC SETTING
3.1  Site Location and Topography
The Package A site is located at 1802 Larchwood Avenue, on the western portion of the Thornbury State
University main campus in Columbus, Ohio. The site is bounded to the north by Larchwood Avenue, to the east
by an existing campus surface parking lot, to the south by an unimproved landscaped strip and to the west by an
existing academic building. The overall Package A footprint is approximately 3.7 acres.
Existing topography varies substantially across 
 Ground surface stands at approximately El. 750.0 ft
across the footprints of Blocks A and C in the northern and eastern portions of 
 Toward the southwest,
across the footprint of Block B, ground surface falls to about El. 738.0 ft (a difference of about 12 ft) in what
appears from historical aerial photography to have been a surface drainage swale draining the pre-development
ground westward toward a former off-site low area. The transition between the two elevations is gradual across
a nominal 60 to 80 ft width. Existing ground within Block B is generally covered with a thin (~0.5 to 1 ft)
mantle of soft organic-rich silty topsoil overlying the SP-SM upper sand; no fill of engineering significance is
present beneath Block B in its current condition.
3.2  Regional and Local Geology
Columbus, Ohio lies within the Till Plains section of the Central Lowland physiographic province. Regional
surficial geology is dominated by Wisconsinan-age glacial deposits — chiefly clay-rich till, glaciolacustrine silt
and clay, and outwash sand and gravel — overlying Devonian-age carbonate and shale bedrock. Local
hydrogeology is characterized by a shallow phreatic surface within the outwash and reworked outwash sands, a
laterally continuous fine-grained aquitard, and a lower confined aquifer within basal outwash sand and gravel
above bedrock.
The subsurface conditions encountered in the Package A borings are consistent with this regional framework: a
medium-dense reworked outwash sand at the surface, a low-permeability clay of glaciolacustrine origin at
intermediate depth, and a dense outwash sand and gravel aquifer at depth. Bedrock was not encountered within
the maximum boring depth of 90 ft (approximately El. 660.0). Blow counts in the SW-GW below El. 720.0
were consistently in the range N ≥ 50 blows per 6 inches, indicating a very dense sand-and-gravel deposit
suitable as a pile-bearing stratum.
3.3  Site History and Prior Use
Site historical review — including review of Franklin County parcel records, USGS topographic maps (1955
and later editions), and Thornbury State University campus master planning archives — indicates that the
Package A parcel was in agricultural use through approximately 1958, was acquired by the University in 1962,
and has been used for surface parking and landscape maintenance since. No prior structures of consequence, no
known below-grade utilities (other than a single abandoned 6-inch clay drain traced along the historic swale in
Block B), and no known industrial fill are present within the footprint. Because there is essentially no prior fill

clay-upper-sand contact after removal of the topsoil mantle — to bring the site to design grade.

for typical foundation details, reinforcement schedules, and standard sections. Refer to architectural sheet A-501 for
below-grade waterproofing details at foundation walls, wall-to-mat construction joints, and slab-on-grade terminations.

concrete or reinforcement.

Outlined on plan within Block B footprint between grids H–L / 3–5 for information. Excavation to be performed under a

Pile type: closed-end pipe piles, driven.

Tip elevation range: El. 686 to El. 690 (bearing in dense sand and gravel stratum below El. 720.0).

Pile layout: see dot pattern on Block B plan (grids B–L / 1–5). Spacing, caps, reinforcement — see S-201/3 (typical pile

Pile driving records: Rowan Bay Constructors submittal package. Capacity basis: SEOR calculations (Calloway
Braddock).
BLOCK C — SPREAD FOOTINGS
Block C is founded on spread footings bearing above compressible clay. No basement is constructed beneath Block C.
Foundation type: isolated and combined spread footings.
Bearing stratum: upper sand / topsoil-stripped clay per Geotechnical Report.
Design bearing pressure: see typical spread footing S-201/3.

Column grid: B–L / 6–8.

log for status.
COLUMN GRID

locations.

1. PURPOSE AND SCOPE
This memorandum establishes the governing codes, reference standards, site parameters, design loads, load
combinations, and serviceability criteria adopted for the structural design of Package A of the Birchwood Village
Expansion. Package A comprises three student-housing blocks (Blocks A, B and C) constructed over a shared
podium, one basement level beneath Blocks A and B, and a separate deep plant-room excavation planned beneath
Block B. The design basis stated herein governs all Package A calculations, drawings, and specifications issued
by the Engineer of Record and controls the interpretation of subordinate design documents where a conflict
arises.
This Rev.2 issue supersedes Rev.1 dated 07/18/2025. Substantive changes since Rev.1 are recorded in the
Revision Block on the final page.
2. GOVERNING CODES AND REFERENCE STANDARDS
The Project is designed in accordance with the following:
• Ohio Building Code (2024 edition, adopting IBC 2021 with Ohio amendments) — governing building
code as adopted by the State of Ohio; Chapter 16 (Structural Design) references ASCE 7-16 for loads.
• ACI 318-19, Building Code Requirements for Structural Concrete and Commentary — reinforced concrete
design, detailing, cover, and serviceability.
• ASCE 7-16, Minimum Design Loads and Associated Criteria for Buildings and Other Structures — dead,
live, snow, wind, seismic loads and load combinations.
• AISC 360-16, Specification for Structural Steel Buildings — structural steel members and connections at
podium framing and roof.
• ACI 301-20 for cast-in-place concrete construction requirements referenced through Spec 03 30 00.
• ASCE 32-01 for frost-protected shallow foundations where applicable at Block C perimeter.
Materials and test methods are governed by the specifications listed in Section 03 20 00, 03 30 00, and 31 20 00
(Rev.2, current at the date of this memorandum), and where cited by ASTM designation on the drawings.

standard, the more stringent provision governs unless the Ohio amendment expressly modifies the standard.

Strength design (LRFD) load combinations for gravity, wind, and seismic follow ASCE 7-16 §2.3.1. Allowable
stress combinations (ASD) per §2.4 are used only for soil-structure interaction checks at the geotechnical
interface (bearing pressure, settlement) and are stated in the geotechnical calculation package. Load combinations
relevant to Package A are set out in full below.
6.1 Basic Strength Load Combinations — ASCE 7-16 §2.3.1
(1)  1.4D
(2)  1.2D + 1.6L + 0.5(Lr or S or R)

compounds) the effect of the variable load.

A.   Testing Laboratory. Field and laboratory testing under this Section shall be performed by the
Owner's independent construction materials testing laboratory (the “Laboratory”), contracted
directly to the Owner. The Contractor shall coordinate access, sampling opportunity, and
lift-by-lift notification with the Laboratory.
B.   Personnel. Nuclear-gauge operators shall hold current radiation safety training and shall be
documented as competent in ASTM D6938 direct-transmission procedures. Nuclear gauges
shall be calibrated within the manufacturer's stated interval and standard-count checked at
the start of each testing day.
C.   Placed-Material Correspondence. The laboratory maximum dry density and optimum
moisture content used as the acceptance denominators for any test location shall be those
determined by ASTM D1557 Method C on the material actually placed at that location. Where
the placed material differs materially from the previously characterized borrow, a new ASTM
D1557 Method C test shall be performed on the new material before further fill placement is
accepted.
1.5   SUBMITTALS
A.   Prior to structural fill placement, submit for review:
1.   Source identification for each proposed borrow, including gradation (sieve analysis),
Atterberg limits, and USCS classification.
2.   Laboratory report of maximum dry density and optimum moisture content per ASTM
D1557 Method C for each proposed source material.
3.   Placement and compaction plan identifying lift thickness, compaction equipment, and
passes.
B.   During placement, submit daily:

1.   Field density reports per ASTM D6938 identifying test location, lift number, elevation, dry
density, moisture content, the ASTM D1557 Method C laboratory maximum dry density
and optimum moisture content used as denominators, percent compaction, and moisture
deviation from optimum.
1.6   SEQUENCING
A.   No structural fill shall be placed until the underlying subgrade has been proof-rolled in the
presence of the Laboratory and accepted in writing by the Owner's Representative Engineer.
B.   No fill placement shall proceed on any lift until the preceding lift has been tested and
accepted per Article 3.4.
PART 2    PRODUCTS
2.1   STRUCTURAL FILL
A.   Material. Well-graded granular fill classified SM or SW-SM, laboratory-tested per ASTM
D1557 Method C (modified Proctor) prior to placement.
B.   Gradation. Structural fill shall meet the following gradation, with no more than 12% passing
the No. 200 sieve and a plasticity index not exceeding 6.
C.   Deleterious Material. Structural fill shall be free of organic material, frozen soil, debris, and
particles greater than 3 inches in largest dimension.
D.   Laboratory Characterization. For each source and for each material change, the Laboratory
shall determine the maximum dry density and optimum moisture content by ASTM D1557
Method C prior to placement. The resulting laboratory values are the denominators against
which the acceptance criteria of Article 3.4.B are evaluated.
2.2   COMMON FILL
A.   Common fill placed outside the building envelope shall be free of organic material, debris, and
frozen soil, but is not subject to the acceptance criteria of Article 3.4.B.
2.3   CAPILLARY BREAK / DRAINAGE COURSE
A.   Clean, open-graded crushed stone, 3/4 in nominal, less than 2% passing the No. 200 sieve,
placed as shown on the Drawings beneath slabs-on-grade.
PART 3    EXECUTION
3.1   EXAMINATION
A.   Examine subgrade prior to fill placement. Do not proceed with fill placement over subgrade
that is soft, yielding under proof roll, frozen, or otherwise unsuitable. Notify the Owner's
Representative Engineer in writing of any unsuitable subgrade condition.
3.2   SUBGRADE PREPARATION
A.   Strip topsoil, organic material, and any existing uncontrolled fill from beneath the footprint of
structural fill.
B.   Proof-roll exposed subgrade with a loaded tandem-axle dump truck or equivalent equipment
approved in writing by the Owner's Representative Engineer. The Laboratory shall be present

--- page 4 ---
to witness the proof roll.
C.   Undercut and replace yielding areas with structural fill placed and compacted per this
Section.
3.3   PLACEMENT
A.   Place structural fill in horizontal lifts not exceeding 12 inches loose thickness.
B.   Moisture-condition each lift, by wetting or drying and mixing, so that the moisture content at
the time of compaction is within the range specified in Article 3.4.B.
C.   Compact each lift with equipment sized and operated to achieve the density and moisture
requirements of Article 3.4.B throughout the full thickness of the lift.
D.   Do not place fill on frozen subgrade or with frozen material. Do not place fill during
precipitation that raises the placed material's moisture content above the upper limit of Article
3.4.B.
3.4   COMPACTION
A.   Method Statement. The Contractor shall place structural fill in controlled lifts as specified in
Article 3.3, moisture-conditioning each lift as necessary to bring the material within the
moisture range required by Article 3.4.B before compaction. Compaction equipment
(self-propelled vibratory smooth-drum rollers, pad-foot rollers, or plate compactors adjacent to
structures) shall be operated in a pattern of overlapping passes such that every location
within a lift receives no fewer than the number of passes established during a
Contractor-conducted test strip witnessed by the Laboratory and the Owner's Representative
Engineer. The test strip shall be executed at the start of production placement, using the
placement source, moisture-conditioning method, lift thickness, and compaction equipment
intended for production, and shall demonstrate that the criteria of Article 3.4.B are met before
general production is authorized. Adjacent to walls, columns, and utilities, use hand-operated
compaction equipment in lifts not exceeding 6 inches loose thickness. Do not operate heavy
compaction equipment within 3 feet of walls prior to backfill balancing on both sides. Each lift
shall be tested and accepted per Article 3.4.B before the next lift is placed.
B.   Acceptance Criteria.
Structural fill shall be placed and compacted to a dry density of not less than
95% of the maximum dry density determined by ASTM D1557 Method C for the
placed material, AND shall be placed at a moisture content within −1% to +2%
of the optimum moisture content determined by the same test. Both criteria must
be satisfied for each test location. Field density shall be measured per ASTM
D6938 (nuclear gauge, direct-transmission mode) at a frequency of one test per
5,000 sf per lift.
C.   Failing Tests. Where either the density criterion or the moisture criterion of Article 3.4.B is
not satisfied at any test location:
1.   The affected area of the lift shall be reworked (scarified, moisture-conditioned, and
recompacted, or removed and replaced) at the Contractor's expense.
2.   Reworked areas shall be retested by the Laboratory. Both the density and moisture
criteria of Article 3.4.B must be satisfied on the retest before the lift is accepted.

3.   Isolated failing tests may not be averaged with adjacent passing tests to demonstrate
compliance. Acceptance is evaluated at each test location independently.
D.   Interpretation. No test location shall be accepted on the basis of density alone. No test
location shall be accepted on the basis of moisture alone. Compliance requires that both the
density criterion and the moisture criterion of Article 3.4.B be independently satisfied at that
test location, as measured against the ASTM D1557 Method C laboratory maximum dry
density and optimum moisture content of the material actually placed at that location.
3.5   BACKFILL AGAINST FOUNDATION WALLS
A.   Do not commence backfill against basement or foundation walls until the wall has attained its
specified 28-day compressive strength, or until permanent lateral support (floor framing) is in
place and grouted to the wall, whichever occurs first.
B.   Place backfill on both sides of interior walls in balanced lifts not exceeding 12 inches loose
thickness, differing by no more than one lift side-to-side.
C.   Compact backfill to the same acceptance criteria as Article 3.4.B where the backfill supports
structure or slabs; elsewhere, to 90% of ASTM D1557 Method C maximum dry density.
3.6   SETTLEMENT TOLERANCE
A.   Total and Differential Settlement. Total settlement 1.0 in maximum; differential settlement
0.5 in maximum over 30 ft.
B.   Application. The tolerances of Paragraph A apply to the completed foundation system as
constructed on the accepted subgrade and structural fill delivered under this Section. Where
predicted or monitored settlements exceed the tolerances of Paragraph A, the Structural
Engineer of Record shall be notified in writing and no additional load shall be applied until a
written disposition is issued.
C.   Monitoring. Where settlement monitoring points are shown on the Drawings, readings shall
be taken and transmitted to the Owner's Representative Engineer at the frequency indicated.
Cumulative settlement approaching either tolerance of Paragraph A shall be reported
immediately.
3.7   FIELD QUALITY CONTROL
A.   Testing frequency for structural fill:
1.   In-place density and moisture: one ASTM D6938 test per 5,000 sf per lift, as required by
Article 3.4.B, and not fewer than three tests per lift regardless of lift area.
2.   Laboratory maximum dry density and optimum moisture content: one ASTM D1557
Method C determination per source, and one additional determination for each material
change identified by visual classification or gradation.
B.   Reporting. The Laboratory shall issue field density reports within 24 hours of testing. Each
report shall identify, for each test location, the ASTM D1557 Method C laboratory maximum
dry density and optimum moisture content used as the denominators, the measured dry
density, the measured moisture content, the percent compaction, the moisture deviation from
optimum, and the disposition (accept or reject) against Article 3.4.B.
C.   Non-Conforming Work. Any lift not meeting Article 3.4.B, or any lift for which the ASTM
D1557 Method C denominators used in reporting do not correspond to the material actually
placed, shall be reworked as required by Article 3.4.C before any additional lift is placed.

1. Purpose and Scope
This field observation report documents excavation observations, groundwater monitoring readings and seepage
observations recorded by Kelbrook Geotechnical field personnel across the Package A footprint over the
construction period 07/2025 through 05/2026. The observations reported herein are drawn from the writer’s
daily field notes, from the shallow standpipe and deep piezometer monitoring log maintained under the ongoing
Package A groundwater monitoring program, and from photographs and sketches taken at the time of
observation. The report is furnished in support of the Owner’s Representative construction verification file and
as supplemental record to the Geotechnical Investigation Report Rev.2 (KGI-2024-0417).
Two distinct field episodes are documented: (a) the Block A basement excavation, opened in the summer of
2025 to a working subgrade at approximately El. 730.0; and (b) the placement of engineered fill across the
Block B footprint from 10/06/2025 through 11/02/2025 and the subsequent months of pile installation and
lift-up to design grade. Groundwater monitoring is continuous across both episodes and is reported in full.
2. Excavation Observations — Block A Basement
2.1 Excavation Opening and Progression
Adrian Vance


--- page 2 ---
Kelbrook Geotechnical, Inc.
Report No. KGI-FO-2026-0528
Field Observation Report — Excavation and Groundwater — Package A
Page 2
The Block A basement excavation was opened in the northeast quadrant of the Package A footprint on
07/14/2025 and progressed from existing grade El. 750.0 down to a working subgrade at approximately El.
730.0 (approximately one foot below the design underside of the basement mat at El. 731.5, to accommodate a
lean-concrete working mat). The excavation was carried out by the Contractor using a mid-size hydraulic
excavator with side dumping to trucks; sequence proceeded from the east perimeter westward across the Block
A footprint over the course of approximately three weeks.
Perimeter shoring — a combination of soldier pile and timber lagging along the northern and eastern faces, and
open-cut battered slopes along the interior (Block A / Block B transition) — was installed ahead of the cut face.
Well-point dewatering, executed per the Contractor’s Dewatering and Groundwater Control Plan Rev.1
dated 06/04/2025, was activated on 07/12/2025, two days before the first cut, and remained in operation
continuously through mat placement on 01/12/2026 and thereafter to protect the wall pour sequence.
2.2 Side Conditions Observed in the Cut Face
Exposed cut faces along the Block A perimeter revealed the following, consistent with the strata described in
Section 6 of the reference report:
•
From existing grade El. 750.0 down to approximately El. 746.0: approximately 4 ft of loose topsoil,
root-mat and reworked surface fill of engineering significance limited to the upper 0.5 to 1 ft, transitioning
downward into weathered upper sand. This layer was over-excavated and hauled off-site as unsuitable for
structural fill re-use.
•
From approximately El. 746.0 down to El. 738.0: the SP-SM upper sand — medium-dense, moist above
the water table and saturated below it, with a modest silt content and no interbedded fine-grained seams.
Cut face stability in the sand above the water table was satisfactory at 1H:1V; below the water table (once
dewatered) the face was cut vertically against the shoring without slumping.
•
From El. 738.0 down to the working subgrade at El. 730.0: the top of the CL clay aquitard, exposed as
a stiff, medium-plasticity lean clay of grey-brown colour. The top of the clay at El. 738.0 was consistent
within ± 0.5 ft across the Block A footprint. The clay retained a vertical or near-vertical face for the
excavation duration without noticeable creep or heave; subgrade compaction footprint (proof-rolling)
produced no rutting or pumping under the loaded haul truck used for the check.
The transition from Stratum 1 (upper sand) to Stratum 2 (clay) at El. 738.0 was sharp and well-defined in the cut
face and matched the elevation logged in Borings B-01, B-02, B-07 and B-09 within a few tenths of a foot.
2.3 Working Subgrade Condition
Subgrade at El. 730.0 was inspected on 08/06/2025 in the presence of the Contractor’s Superintendent (Mr.
Marcus Whitfield) and the Owner’s Representative (Mr. 
). Subgrade was found to be firm,
uniform, free of standing water within the dewatered footprint, and suitable to receive the lean-concrete
working mat and subsequently the reinforced mat foundation. No soft spots, disturbed zones or unsuitable
inclusions were logged. The subgrade approval memorandum was issued separately by Kelbrook on
08/07/2025.
3. Groundwater Monitoring — Continuous Record
Groundwater monitoring under the Package A program continues from the piezometer array installed
11/22/2024 and reported in the Geotechnical Investigation Report Rev.2. Over the observation period 07/2025
rounds since installation. Readings are taken monthly (weekly during active excavation and dewatering).
through 05/2026 an additional eleven monitoring rounds were completed, bringing the total record to eighteen
Adrian Vance


--- page 3 ---
Kelbrook Geotechnical, Inc.
Report No. KGI-FO-2026-0528
Field Observation Report — Excavation and Groundwater — Package A
Page 3
3.1 Design Water Table — Upper Sand (Shallow Standpipe Piezometers)
The design water table in the upper SP-SM sand, established at El. 742.0 in the reference report, is confirmed
by the extended monitoring record. Readings from the three shallow standpipe piezometers (B-01, B-03, B-09),
taken across the 07/2025 through 05/2026 observation period at locations outside the Block A dewatered
footprint, remain in the range El. 741.6 to El. 742.4, with individual monthly means clustered within a few
tenths of a foot of El. 742.0. No systematic trend, no seasonal excursion beyond that range and no departure
from the design elevation was recorded.
3.2 Confined Piezometric Head — Deep Aquifer (Deep Piezometers)
The confined piezometric head in the deep SW-GW sand-and-gravel aquifer below El. 720.0, established at El.
738.0 in the reference report, is likewise confirmed. Readings from the two deep piezometers (B-04 and B-08),
both screened below El. 720.0 within the Block B footprint, remain in the range El. 737.7 to El. 738.3 across
the full extended record. The head is stable, without trend, and consistent with the value carried forward from
the Rev.2 investigation.

Both regimes — the shallow phreatic surface at El. 742.0 in the upper sands and the confined piezometric head
at El. 738.0 in the deep aquifer below El. 720.0 — remain consistent with KGI-2024-0417 Rev.2. The
eighteen-foot separation between the top of the clay aquitard and the top of the deep aquifer continues to isolate
the two regimes.
4. Seepage Observations — Block A Excavation and Dewatering Response
4.1 Seepage into the Cut Face
During the Block A basement excavation, groundwater seepage was observed entering the excavation at the
exposed cut face where the upper SP-SM sand was cut below the design water table. Seepage was concentrated
at elevations El. 741.8 to El. 742.2, corresponding to the top of the phreatic surface in the upper sand. The
seepage was clear (non-turbid after brief initial flushing), sustained rather than intermittent, and distributed
along the cut face rather than emerging from a discrete conduit or seam. No seepage was observed emerging
from the top of the CL clay at El. 738.0; the clay presented no visible cracks or fissures and no seepage exit
points at or below its exposed face.
The observed seepage elevations (El. 741.8 to El. 742.2) reproduce the range recorded in exploratory
test-pitting during the original 2024 investigation and are consistent with the shallow standpipe piezometer
readings from stations outside the dewatered footprint (Section 3.1). The two independent measurements —
piezometer standpipe readings and cut-face seepage entry — corroborate each other and confirm the design
water table elevation.


--- page 4 ---
Kelbrook Geotechnical, Inc.
Report No. KGI-FO-2026-0528
Field Observation Report — Excavation and Groundwater — Package A
Page 4
4.2 Well-Point Dewatering Response — Upper Sand
Well-point dewatering, executed per the Contractor’s Dewatering and Groundwater Control Plan Rev.1
was operated continuously across the Block A footprint from 07/12/2025 through the mat placement
date and beyond. Piezometer readings taken from a spare standpipe drop set inside the dewatered perimeter, in
combination with well-point riser inspections, showed the upper sand water level drawn down to approximately
El. 728 within the dewatered perimeter — approximately 14 feet below the ambient design water table and
approximately 2 feet below the working subgrade at El. 730.0. Drawdown within the perimeter was achieved
within approximately 48 hours of well-point activation and was maintained at that level throughout the
excavation and mat construction window.
The dewatering system performed as designed for the shallow phreatic surface in the upper sand across the
Block A footprint. Cut faces below the ambient water table, once well-point drawdown was established,
presented no free seepage during the balance of the mat construction sequence.
4.3 Deep Piezometer Response — Confirms Confined Aquifer Independence
Deep piezometer readings from B-04 and B-08 (both screened in the deep SW-GW aquifer below El. 720.0 and
located within the Block A / Block B footprint) were taken throughout the Block A dewatering campaign.
Across the full period of well-point operation, both deep piezometers continued to read within the range El.
737.7 to El. 738.3, with individual monthly means at or within a few tenths of El. 738.0.
Deep piezometer readings within the Block A footprint were unaffected by upper-sand well-point dewatering.
The upper sand and the deep aquifer are separated by the 18-ft-thick CL clay aquitard from El. 738.0 down to
El. 720.0, and the well-point system draws only from the upper sand. The observed independence of the two
regimes during active dewatering directly confirms the confined character of the deep aquifer and the aquitard
behaviour of the clay, as characterized in the reference report.
5. Notes on Block B — Engineered Fill Placement and Subsequent Monitoring
5.1 Engineered Fill Placement, 10/06/2025 through 11/02/2025
Engineered fill was placed across the Block B footprint over the period 10/06/2025 through 11/02/2025 to bring
the site from natural ground at approximately El. 738.0 up to design grade at El. 750.0 — a nominal 12 ft of fill
in 14 controlled lifts. Fill was placed directly on the stripped clay surface after removal of the surface topsoil
mantle, in accordance with the recommendations of Section 9.5 of the reference report. Compaction and
moisture control were performed under the independent Laboratory’s field density testing program (Vantree
Materials Testing, LLC); the writer’s observations here are limited to the geotechnical monitoring associated
with the underlying strata.
5.2 Deep Piezometer Readings Through Fill Placement, Pile Driving and Subsequent Months
The two deep piezometers B-04 and B-08 are located within the Block B footprint (B-04 within the plant-room
excavation footprint, B-08 adjacent to the basement mat perimeter beneath Blocks A and B, both screened in
the deep aquifer below El. 720.0). Both remained instrumented and readable through fill placement, through
pile installation from 11/06/2025 through 11/21/2025, and through the subsequent months of the observation
period.
Across the entire sequence — before, during and after fill placement; before, during and after pile driving; and

exit_code=0
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""AHPELE requirement scanner (stdlib only; runs inside the task container).

Finds requirement-like statements in the text corpus written by
ahpele_index.py (/tmp/ahpele/corpus) so that hard constraints are not missed:

  python3 ahpele_reqscan.py            # scan: writes /tmp/ahpele/req_candidates.md and .csv
  python3 ahpele_reqscan.py --check    # coverage: lists candidates not yet reviewed
  python3 ahpele_reqscan.py --register FILE.csv|.xlsx   # register rows: is each value in the document it cites?

A candidate counts as reviewed when its ID (e.g. R0042) appears in
/tmp/ahpele/requirements.csv (adopted) or /tmp/ahpele/rejected.csv (rejected,
with a reason). A whole document can be rejected by putting its path in
rejected.csv. The scanner is a recall aid: it misses requirements that live in
tables, drawings or images, and it lists many statements that are not hard
requirements. It knows nothing about any particular task.
"""
import argparse
import csv
import html
import json
import os
import re
import sys

OUT = "/tmp/ahpele"
STRONG = re.compile(
    r"\b(shall|must|is required|are required|required to|mandatory|not permitted|prohibited|shall not|"
    r"must not|may not exceed|no later than|condition of|subject to|is to|are to|(is|are)? ?limited to|"
    r"not (be )?(less|more|greater|lower|higher) than|not exceed|at least|at most|no more than|no less than|"
    r"maximum of|minimum of|is not allowed|are not allowed|will not be accepted|not acceptable)\b", re.I)
LIMIT = re.compile(
    r"(\b(not (to )?exceed|exceed(s|ing)?|maximum|minimum|max\.?|min\.?|at least|at most|no more than|"
    r"no less than|not less than|not more than|not greater than|up to|limit(ed|s)?|cap(ped)?|allowable|"
    r"permissible|permitted|threshold|tolerance|deadline|before|prior to|within|until|expires?|valid)\b|"
    r"[≤≥<>]=?|±|\+/-)", re.I)
NUMBER = re.compile(r"(?<![A-Za-z])[-+]?\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d+)?")
NOISE = re.compile(r"^(--- page \d+ ---|page \d+( of \d+)?|\W*)$", re.I)
MAX_LEN = 320
TAG = re.compile(r"<[^<>]{1,400}>")
# folders that usually hold general reference material (codes, standards, catalogues) rather than project documents
REFERENCE = re.compile(r"(^|/)(library|libraries|reference|references|standards?|codes?|regulations?|catalogues?|"
                       r"catalogs?|vendor|manufacturer)(/|$)", re.I)
# file names of published codes and standards (general engineering knowledge, not task-specific)
STANDARD_NAME = re.compile(
    r"^(\d+[ _-]?CFR|UFC|UFGS|UFM|ASCE|SEI|ACI|AISC|AISI|SDI|SJI|IBC|IRC|IFC[ _-]?\d|IECC|IEC|IEEE|NFPA|NEC|NESC|ISO|EN|"
    r"BS|ASTM|ASHRAE|ASME|AWS|AWWA|API|ANSI|UL|CSA|DIN|AS|NZS|TIA|FM|NEMA|OSHA|EPA|FEMA|AASHTO|MUTCD|ICC|NCHRP|"
    r"USACE|EM[ _-]\d|ETL|DoD|IS)[ _-]?\d", re.I)
DATA_TYPES = {"csv", "json"}
VOID_DIR = re.compile(r"(^|/)(archive[sd]?|superseded|obsolete|old|void|withdrawn|cancell?ed)(/|$)", re.I)


def load_inventory():
    try:
        with open(os.path.join(OUT, "inventory.json"), encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            return {r["path"]: r for r in json.load(fh).get("files", [])}
    except (OSError, ValueError):
        return {}


def statements(text):
    """Yield (page, statement) pairs: lines joined into sentences, table rows kept whole."""
    page, buf = 1, []
    for raw in text.splitlines():
        m = re.match(r"--- page (\d+) ---", raw.strip())
        if m:
            if buf:
                yield page, " ".join(buf)
                buf = []
            page = int(m.group(1))
            continue
        line = raw.strip()
        if NOISE.match(line):
            if buf:
                yield page, " ".join(buf)
                buf = []
            continue
        if "\t" in raw or " | " in line or line.count("  ") > 2:  # table-like row
            if buf:
                yield page, " ".join(buf)
                buf = []
            yield page, re.sub(r"\s+", " ", line)
            continue
        buf.append(line)
        if re.search(r"[.;:]$", line) or len(" ".join(buf)) > 600:
            yield page, " ".join(buf)
            buf = []
    if buf:
        yield page, " ".join(buf)


def split_sentences(s):
    parts = re.split(r"(?<=[.;])\s+(?=[A-Z(])", s)
    return [p.strip() for p in parts if p.strip()]


def scan():
    corpus = os.path.join(OUT, "corpus")
    inv = load_inventory()
    rows = []
    data_like = {d for d, r in inv.items() if r.get("type") in DATA_TYPES}
    for dp, _, fns in os.walk(corpus):
        for fn in sorted(fns):
            if not fn.endswith(".txt"):
                continue
            full = os.path.join(dp, fn)
            doc = os.path.relpath(full, corpus)[:-4]
            try:
                text = open(full, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
            except OSError:
                continue
            if text.count("<") > 20 and len(TAG.findall(text[:20000])) > 20:  # XML / HTML: keep the text only
                text = html.unescape(TAG.sub(lambda m: "\n" if re.match(r"</?(p|div|tr|li|h\d|head|br|section|para)\b",
                                                                     m.group(0), re.I) else " ", text))
            seen = set()
            for page, st in statements(text):
                for s in split_sentences(st):
                    strong, limit, nums = bool(STRONG.search(s)), bool(LIMIT.search(s)), NUMBER.findall(s)
                    if not (strong or (limit and nums)) or (doc in data_like and not strong):
                        continue
                    key = s.lower()[:200]
                    if key in seen or len(s) < 12:
                        continue
                    seen.add(key)
                    score = (4 if nums else 3) if strong else 2  # 4: modal + number, 3: modal, 2: limit + number
                    rows.append({"doc": doc, "page": page, "score": score,
                                 "text": s if len(s) <= MAX_LEN else s[:MAX_LEN] + "…",
                                 "numbers": " ".join(nums[:8])})
    for r in rows:
        r["ref"] = bool(REFERENCE.search(os.path.dirname(r["doc"]))
                        or STANDARD_NAME.search(os.path.basename(r["doc"])))
    rows.sort(key=lambda r: (r["ref"], r["doc"], r["page"]))
    for i, r in enumerate(rows, 1):
        r["id"] = f"R{i:04d}"
    with open(os.path.join(OUT, "req_candidates.csv"), "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        w = csv.DictWriter(fh, fieldnames=["id", "doc", "page", "score", "ref", "numbers", "text"])
        w.writeheader()
        w.writerows(rows)
    by_doc = {}
    for r in rows:
        by_doc.setdefault(r["doc"], []).append(r)
    lines = ["# Requirement candidates", "",
             f"{len(rows)} requirement-like statements in {len(by_doc)} documents (score 4: shall/must/"
             "not-more-than wording with a number; 3: the same wording without a number; 2: a limit word with a "
             "number, often context rather than a requirement). Tables, drawings and scanned pages are only partly covered: "
             "read those yourself. Status flags come from the FILE NAME; confirm which documents govern. Project "
             "documents come first; published codes and standards and documents in reference folders are listed "
             "last: the clauses that apply are the ones the project documents invoke. --check asks you to review the "
             "score 3-4 statements of project documents; use the rest when you look a requirement up.", ""]
    shown_ref = False
    for doc, rs in by_doc.items():
        if rs[0]["ref"] and not shown_ref:
            lines += ["# Reference folders (codes, standards, catalogues)", ""]
            shown_ref = True
        flags = inv.get(doc, {}).get("flags", "")
        lines.append(f"## {doc}" + (f"  [name flags: {flags}]" if flags else "") + f"  ({len(rs)})")
        for r in rs:
            lines.append(f"- {r['id']} p{r['page']} s{r['score']}: {r['text']}")
        lines.append("")
    with open(os.path.join(OUT, "req_candidates.md"), "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        fh.write("\n".join(lines) + "\n")
    key = [r for r in rows if must_review(r)]
    kdocs = {}
    for r in key:
        kdocs[r["doc"]] = kdocs.get(r["doc"], 0) + 1
    top = sorted(kdocs.items(), key=lambda kv: -kv[1])[:10]
    print(f"requirement scan: {len(rows)} candidates in {len(by_doc)} documents -> {OUT}/req_candidates.md; "
          f"{len(key)} strong candidates in project documents to review"
          + (" (" + ", ".join(f"{d}: {n}" for d, n in top) + ")" if top else ""))
    return rows


def must_review(r):
    """Requirement wording (shall, must, is to, not more than ...) in project documents."""
    return int(r["score"]) >= 3 and str(r["ref"]) not in ("True", "1")


def read_text(path):
    try:
        return open(path, encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").read()
    except OSError:
        return ""


def check(limit):
    path = os.path.join(OUT, "req_candidates.csv")
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        scan()
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        rows = list(csv.DictReader(fh))
    adopted = read_text(os.path.join(OUT, "requirements.csv"))
    rejected = read_text(os.path.join(OUT, "rejected.csv"))
    if not adopted.strip():
        print(f"{OUT}/requirements.csv is missing or empty: build the requirements table first "
              "(one row per hard requirement, with the candidate IDs it comes from).")
    ids = set(re.findall(r"\bR\d{4}\b", adopted + "\n" + rejected))
    rejected_docs = {r["doc"] for r in rows if r["doc"] in rejected}
    inv = load_inventory()
    key = [r for r in rows if must_review(r)]

    def covered(r):
        if r["id"] in ids:
            return True
        if r["doc"] not in rejected_docs:
            return False
        # rejecting a whole document covers its statements with a number only when the document is marked void

---
name: engineering-deliverables
description: Method for engineering design and calculation packages graded against requirements - document precedence, superseded documents, requirement/constraint registers, hard-constraint checks, unit discipline, optimisation within constraints, and schema-exact deliverable files (CSV, JSON, XLSX, ZIP, IFC). Use for any task that asks for calculations, a design, a plan, a schedule, a register or a structured submission.
---

# Engineering deliverables

## 1. Know exactly what is graded
- Copy every deliverable requirement from the instruction into `/tmp/ahpele/checklist.md`: path, file name, format,
  required columns/keys/tokens (exact spelling), units, row granularity ("one row per X and Y"), and any scoring rule.
- The instruction is a data contract. Use its column names, token vocabularies and IDs verbatim. Extra columns are
  usually harmless; missing or renamed ones are not.
- If the instruction states how the work is scored (e.g. hard constraints gate the score, cost objective, recall of a
  register), let that decide where effort goes: never trade a hard constraint for objective value.

## 2. Document precedence and status
- Read the governing specification first: it usually lists which standards, revisions and documents apply.
- Typical precedence (unless the project documents say otherwise): addenda / RFI responses / site instructions issued
  later > specification > drawings > schedules > vendor data > reference standards. Later dated responses override
  earlier ones on the same point.
- A document marked superseded, cancelled, withdrawn, void or draft, or an older revision of a document that exists in
  a newer revision, is not an authority. Do not cite it, do not take values from it. Record in your narrative that you
  saw it and why you set it aside.
- Words like "cancelled" inside a document's text often describe another document. Check before discarding.

## 3. Requirements table and register
- Before designing, list every hard requirement with: id, document, clause/table, requirement, limit value, unit, what
  it binds (which items). Save as `/tmp/ahpele/requirements.csv`.
- Hard requirements include: safety and code limits, permit/authorisation limits (discharge, noise, setbacks),
  capacities (power, flow, head, load), resource caps (equipment, crews, water, budget), milestones and deadlines.
- If a register is a deliverable, build it from this table. Cite real project documents and clauses, not the brief.
  Cite only documents that are in force.

## 4. Calculations
- Work in one unit system internally; convert at the boundary. Keep inputs, intermediate results and units in a script
  (`/tmp/ahpele/calc.py`) so numbers can be recomputed after every change.
- Take every input from a document you can cite; write assumptions down where the documents leave a choice.
- Cross-check: totals equal sums of parts, the same quantity has the same value in every file, schedules respect
  durations and predecessors, quantities respect the caps.

## 5. Build early, then improve
- Produce a complete first version of every deliverable early with conservative choices that satisfy all hard
  requirements, even if it is not optimal. An incomplete or missing file scores nothing.
- Never write placeholders (TBD, NaN, "to be determined") in a numeric field. If a value is genuinely not applicable,
  use the not-applicable convention the instruction allows (often blank, N/A or NONE).

## 6. Verify with code
- Write `/tmp/ahpele/check.py` that loads your deliverable files exactly as written and tests every requirement row and
  every checklist item (columns, tokens, units, ranges, cross-file consistency). Run it after every change.
- Run the format checker: `python3 /tmp/ahpele/bin/ahpele_check.py <deliverable paths>`.
- For CAD/BIM outputs, re-open the file with the standard library you wrote it with and check the entities, property
  sets and attributes the instruction names.
- IFC written by hand (no BIM library): generate it with a small script, not by typing STEP lines. Copy each entity
  pattern from the example file the task provides (or from the schema), keep every attribute in order (use `$` for an
  unset one; an IfcBuildingStorey has 10 attributes, an IfcPropertySet 5, an IfcRelDefinesByProperties 6), write every REAL
  with a decimal point (`20.` or `20.0`, never `20` and never `4.5.`; coordinates, directions, depths, elevations), and double apostrophes inside strings. Run
  `python3 /tmp/ahpele/bin/ahpele_ifc.py <file>` until it reports 0 errors, and compare its structure printout
  (storeys and elevations, property sets, footprints, heights) with what the contract requires. One unreadable
  entity can make the whole file unreadable.
- Placed or routed 3D models (coordination models, MEP routing, layouts): verify the FILE, not your script's variables.
  `python3 /tmp/ahpele/bin/ahpele_clash.py <file.ifc> --point <entry x,y,z>` re-reads it with ifcopenshell's geometry
  engine in world coordinates and lists clashing pairs, element classes stacked at one spot, broken runs and the
  distance from each run to the entry point. Coordinates in `IfcCartesianPoint` are in the project length unit (a
  millimetre project takes millimetres); library helpers such as `ifcopenshell.api` placement calls take SI metres and
  convert for you, so do not divide by 1000 by hand as well. Iterate until 0 clashes and one network per service.

## 7. Optimise last
- Only after all hard checks pass: improve the objective (cost, performance) with a systematic search (enumerate
  options, or scipy.optimize when available), re-running the checks for every candidate. Keep the best feasible plan
  on disk at all times.

name: professional-memo
description: How to write an engineering memo, letter, reply, review response or technical note for a named recipient, written for an expert reader - answer first, basis from the record, every issue with owner and timing, exact scope, signature block, and a correct DOCX file. Use whenever the deliverable is a memo, letter, reply, response, review, disposition or note.
---

# Professional engineering memo

## Before writing
- Identify: who asked, who will act on the memo, the decision they must take, the "as of" date of the record, and any
  dates in the request (target date, deadline). Note what the request says is OUT of scope and leave it out.
- Gather the record: correspondence (emails, letters, RFIs), applications, studies, test reports, standards, contracts,
  tracking data in project applications. Build a dated timeline of relevant events in `/tmp/ahpele/timeline.md`.
- For each potential issue, find the exact source (document, section, date) and what it requires.
- For go/no-go questions (approve, issue, energise, accept, pay), do not stop at the first favourable reading. Build a checklist of every condition that applies
  (agreements, studies, permits, tests, payments, insurance, notices, deadlines, sign-offs, open correspondence) and
  check each one against the record as of the stated date. Only conclude that nothing blocks the decision after every
  condition has been checked and cited.

## Structure
1. Header: To / From / Date (use the record's "as of" date unless told otherwise) / Subject / project identifiers.
2. **Answer first**: one or two sentences that directly answer the question (yes / no / not yet, by which date), with
   the decisive reason.
3. **Basis**: the facts and requirements the answer rests on, each cited to the record (document, section, date).
4. **Open items** (one per issue): what it is; what requirement it rests on (cite it); what has to be done; who must do
   it (name the party or role, including the customer/applicant when it is theirs); whether it can be done before the
   target date and why; consequence if not.
5. Items reviewed and found acceptable, briefly, so the reader knows they were checked.
6. Scope statement: what this memo does not cover, exactly as the request defines it.
7. Recommendation / next steps with dates.
8. Signature block for the reviewing engineer if the request asks for one (name/title placeholders only where the
   request leaves the signer unnamed; never invent credentials).

## Determinations the reader can check
- Make a list of every question and request in the instruction (asks.md) and answer each one in its own labelled place.
- Each answer states the specific fact and the conclusion in one or two plain sentences: "<thing> is / is not <state>,
  because <fact with value and unit> (<document, section/sheet, date>)". Then give the working.
- When the record does not let you decide a question, say exactly what is missing, who must provide it and what the
  decision is meanwhile.
- Commit to one disposition per question, as engineering requests usually ask.
- Name the cause, not only the symptom: when something fails or is non-conforming, state why (which input, assumption,
  revision or condition) and what has to change.

## Scope, states and length
- Keep a scope ledger: what the request asks, what it excludes, what is under someone else's review. Items under separate
  review are mentioned, not decided; items that bear on the answer stay in even if raised elsewhere.
- Check the answer in every operating state or stage the request covers (before / during / after an event, normal and
  abnormal), not only the steady case.
- Length and precision follow the reader: a decision memo is usually 1-3 pages plus attachments; report numbers to the
  precision of the data (not six decimals); match tone and distribution to an internal or external recipient.

## Quality rules
- Be specific: dates, amounts, ratings, section numbers, document titles. No vague hedging.
- Distinguish facts from the record, requirements, and your engineering judgement.
- Check arithmetic and dates (business days, notice periods, expiry dates) with a script.
- Do not contradict yourself between the answer and the open items.
- Claim only actions that were actually taken (a request "has been sent" only if you sent it, with its record);
  otherwise write what should be done and by whom. Each follow-up becomes its own tracked item (ticket, task,
  register line with owner and date), not only a sentence inside a closed record.
- External letters carry no internal matters (internal case numbers, staff deliberations, other customers'
  correspondence, internal directives); keep those in the internal memo.
- Before netting a figure against a published baseline (capacity, budget, allowance), check what that baseline
  already includes and excludes, and say so.

## Producing the file
- Write DOCX with python-docx when available (`import docx`); otherwise use the word processing MCP tool if the task
  provides one, or build the file with LibreOffice (`soffice --headless --convert-to docx file.md` or `.html`).
- Use real headings and tables, not Markdown symbols inside the Word text.
- Save exactly at the path and file name the request gives; re-open the file to confirm it reads back, and run
  `python3 /tmp/ahpele/bin/ahpele_check.py <path>`.
- If the request also asks for actions in project applications (tickets, work packages, emails, calendar), do them
  too, and make their content consistent with the memo (see the workplace-apps skill).
- End with a final message that states the answer and lists every file and record you created.

The review covers the twelve Block C footings (C-1 through C-12) bearing in the upper sand above the CL clay aquitard from El. 738.0 to El. 720.0. 015 | 3.  BASIS OF REVIEW

019 | •	Specification 31 20 00 Rev.3, Article 3.6.C: settlement readings shall be taken and transmitted to the Owner's Representative Engineer at the indicated frequency; cumulative settlement approaching either tolerance shall be reported immediately.
020 | •	Geotechnical Investigation Report Rev.2, Section 8.1: long-term one-dimensional consolidation settlement shall be computed by Sc = Cc·H/(1+e0)·log10[(σ'0+q)/σ'0], with Cc = 0.28, e0 = 0.92, H = 18 ft and σ'0 = 1,850 psf at mid-depth (El. 729.0); σ'p = 1,900 psf (OCR 1.03), so any q above about 50 psf produces virgin compression.
021 | •	Geotechnical Investigation Report Rev.2, Section 9.1: the Structural Engineer of Record must explicitly compute consolidation settlement of the clay under the stress increase q at mid-depth caused by each governing footing, using the Table 5-1 parameters, and reconcile the result against the total-and-differential settlement tolerances.
022 | •	Design Basis Memorandum Rev.2, Section 7.3: Block C settlement is a serviceability check in CB-GEO-007, using the tolerances in Specification 31 20 00 Article 3.6. Section 9: the geotechnical report controls all soil parameters, and any conflict is resolved in favour of that report.
023 | •	ASTM D2435/D2435M-11 (Reapproved 2020): one-dimensional consolidation test method used by Vantree for the clay parameters.
024 | The inputs used in the independent recomputation are listed in Table 2. I applied the stricter reading where the record allows two readings: the 1.0 in limit is applied to total settlement (immediate plus primary plus secondary), not to immediate settlement alone; the 0.5 in differential limit is applied over a 30-ft gauge, not a longer diagonal; and both predicted and monitored settlement are treated as triggers under Article 3.6.B.

027 | Finding 1 — CB-GEO-007 does not compute long-term consolidation; Sheet 4 is blank.
028 | CB-GEO-007 Sheet 4 — Consolidation (rows 6 to 15) is a table of placeholders ("—"). Cell A15 states: "Not computed. Serviceability taken from the immediate settlement result on Sheet 3." The Sheet 3 conclusion (cells A69–A70) is expressly limited to "Immediate elastic settlement ... 0.9 in" and a differential of 0.2 in. The calculation therefore does not compute consolidation of the 18-ft CL clay, although GIR Rev.2 Sections 8.1 and 9.1 require the Structural Engineer of Record to compute it explicitly for each governing footing and reconcile it to the tolerances, and DBM Rev.2 Section 7.3 records that Block C settlement is checked in CB-GEO-007. The omission is the governing long-term mechanism, not a presentation gap: without it, the 0.9 in cannot be compared with the 1.0 in total limit.
029 | Finding 2 — The recomputed long-term consolidation is 5.42 in; total settlement is 6.32 in against a 1.0 in limit.
030 | Using the GIR's own one-dimensional equation and the parameters in Table 2:
031 | Sc = Cc·H/(1+e0)·log10[(σ'0 + Δσ)/σ'0] = 0.28 × 18/(1 + 0.92) × log10[(1,850 + 900)/1,850]
032 | = 2.625 × log10(1.4865) = 0.452 ft = 5.42 in.
033 | Adding the calculated immediate settlement of 0.90 in (CB-GEO-007 Sheet 3 cell G50) gives a total of 6.32 in. The total limit is 1.0 in (Specification 31 20 00 Article 3.6.A), so the utilisation is 6.32; the consolidation component alone is 5.42 times the total limit. If the 50-psf recompression band to σ'p is credited (Cr = 0.045), Sc = 5.12 in and the total is 6.02 in. The EOR must reconcile S-201 Rev.4 with the as-built/monitoring geometry and confirm the geometry used in the revised settlement analysis. The as-built/monitoring geometry is the one I used for the stress-increase check, because it matches the constructed footings; the current drawing conflict is itself a record non-conformance.

040 | At mid-clay El. 729.0, with 12 ft of upper sand at 118 pcf, 9 ft of clay at 120 pcf and the design water table at El. 742.0, the vertical total stress is σv = 12 × 118 + 9 × 120 = 2,496 psf and the pore pressure is u = (742.0 − 729.0) × 62.4 = 811 psf, giving σ'0 = 1,685 psf. GIR Rev.2 Table 5-1 and VMT Summary B14 state 1,850 psf (about 10% higher), but neither document shows the calculation; 1,850 psf is consistent with a water table near El. 739.4, not El. 742.0. Using the lower, profile-derived value increases Sc from 5.42 to 5.86 in (total 6.76 in), so the conclusion is unchanged. 044 | CB-GEO-007 Sheet 3 compares an immediate differential of 0.2 in between F-C6 and F-C12 over a 35.8-ft diagonal with the 0.5-in differential tolerance. 000| THELBRIDGE PROJECT MANAGEMENT SERVICES

001| 500 South High Street, Suite 720, Columbus, OH 43215  |  (614) 555-0125  |  thelbridgepm.com

002| VERIFICATION MEMORANDUM

003| To:	Adrian Vance, Project Engineer (Structural/Geotechnical), Owner's Representative

004| From:	Rahul Nimkar, Geotechnical Reviewer

005| Date:	07/20/2026

006| Subject:	Item 051 — Block C Spread Footings — Long-Term Settlement Verification, Package A

007| cc:	Rachel Marlbeck, University Program Director, Thornbury State University

008| Determination: NOT VERIFIED (design review). Item 051 remains Open. The settlement analysis omits long-term consolidation; the computed total is about 6.3 in against a 1.0 in limit. Revise and resubmit.

009| 1.  PURPOSE

010| This memorandum records Thelbridge's verification review of Item 051 on the Package A Review Comment and Verification Register. Item 051 requires verification of the Block C spread-footing foundations for long-term settlement of the underlying compressible CL clay (Cc = 0.28, e0 = 0.92, σ'p = 1,900 psf; 18 ft layer) under a stress increase Δσ = 900 psf at mid-layer, against the project tolerance of 1.0 in total and 0.5 in differential, and correlation with the 0.61 in cumulative reading of 06/26/2026. The item is due 07/20/2026, two days before the 07/22/2026 Level-3 concrete placement.

011| The question is whether the Block C settlement analysis (CB-GEO-007) is complete and reconciled to the project tolerances, and whether the constructed footings are verified for long-term serviceability. The review covers the twelve Block C footings (C-1 through C-12) bearing in the upper sand above the CL clay aquitard from El. 738.0 to El. 720.0. It does not cover bearing capacity of the upper sand except as a cross-check, the basement mat (Item 050), the Block B piles (Item 049) or the Block B plant-room shoring (Item 048). No RFI or site instruction in the record changes the Block C settlement basis; RFI 104 concerns basement wall-to-mat joints only.

012| 2.  DOCUMENTS REVIEWED

013| The review was made against the following documents, read in the revisions stated. Superseded revisions were identified and are not relied on.

014| Table 1 — Documents reviewed. GIR Rev.1 (12/12/2024) and DBM Rev.1 (07/18/2025) are superseded and were not used. The CB-GEO-007 signed/sealed PDF referenced on its cover was not in the review set; the native Rev.0 workbook was reviewed.

015| 3.  BASIS OF REVIEW

016| The governing requirements applied are:

017| •	Specification 31 20 00 Rev.3, Article 3.6.A: total settlement 1.0 in maximum; differential settlement 0.5 in maximum over 30 ft.

018| •	Specification 31 20 00 Rev.3, Article 3.6.B: where predicted or monitored settlement exceeds either tolerance, the Structural Engineer of Record shall be notified in writing and no additional load shall be applied until a written disposition is issued.

019| •	Specification 31 20 00 Rev.3, Article 3.6.C: settlement readings shall be taken and transmitted to the Owner's Representative Engineer at the indicated frequency; cumulative settlement approaching either tolerance shall be reported immediately.

020| •	Geotechnical Investigation Report Rev.2, Section 8.1: long-term one-dimensional consolidation settlement shall be computed by Sc = Cc·H/(1+e0)·log10[(σ'0+q)/σ'0], with Cc = 0.28, e0 = 0.92, H = 18 ft and σ'0 = 1,850 psf at mid-depth (El. 729.0); σ'p = 1,900 psf (OCR 1.03), so any q above about 50 psf produces virgin compression.

021| •	Geotechnical Investigation Report Rev.2, Section 9.1: the Structural Engineer of Record must explicitly compute consolidation settlement of the clay under the stress increase q at mid-depth caused by each governing footing, using the Table 5-1 parameters, and reconcile the result against the total-and-differential settlement tolerances.

022| •	Design Basis Memorandum Rev.2, Section 7.3: Block C settlement is a serviceability check in CB-GEO-007, using the tolerances in Specification 31 20 00 Article 3.6. Section 9: the geotechnical report controls all soil parameters, and any conflict is resolved in favour of that report.

023| •	ASTM D2435/D2435M-11 (Reapproved 2020): one-dimensional consolidation test method used by Vantree for the clay parameters.

024| The register's reference tab records the 1.0 in / 0.5 in values as descriptive facts from CB-GEO-007; the controlling source is Specification 31 20 00 Rev.3 Article 3.6.A, which the DBM also cites. The inputs used in the independent recomputation are listed in Table 2. I applied the stricter reading where the record allows two readings: the 1.0 in limit is applied to total settlement (immediate plus primary plus secondary), not to immediate settlement alone; the 0.5 in differential limit is applied over a 30-ft gauge, not a longer diagonal; and both predicted and monitored settlement are treated as triggers under Article 3.6.B.

025| Table 2 — Inputs used in the independent recomputation, with their record source.

026| 4.  FINDINGS

027| Finding 1 — CB-GEO-007 does not compute long-term consolidation; Sheet 4 is blank.

028| CB-GEO-007 Sheet 4 — Consolidation (rows 6 to 15) is a table of placeholders ("—"). Cell A15 states: "Not computed. Serviceability taken from the immediate settlement result on Sheet 3." The Sheet 3 conclusion (cells A69–A70) is expressly limited to "Immediate elastic settlement ... 0.9 in" and a differential of 0.2 in. The calculation therefore does not compute consolidation of the 18-ft CL clay, although GIR Rev.2 Sections 8.1 and 9.1 require the Structural Engineer of Record to compute it explicitly for each governing footing and reconcile it to the tolerances, and DBM Rev.2 Section 7.3 records that Block C settlement is checked in CB-GEO-007. The omission is the governing long-term mechanism, not a presentation gap: without it, the 0.9 in cannot be compared with the 1.0 in total limit.

029| Finding 2 — The recomputed long-term consolidation is 5.42 in; total settlement is 6.32 in against a 1.0 in limit.

030| Using the GIR's own one-dimensional equation and the parameters in Table 2:

031| Sc = Cc·H/(1+e0)·log10[(σ'0 + Δσ)/σ'0] = 0.28 × 18/(1 + 0.92) × log10[(1,850 + 900)/1,850]

032| = 2.625 × log10(1.4865) = 0.452 ft = 5.42 in.

033| Adding the calculated immediate settlement of 0.90 in (CB-GEO-007 Sheet 3 cell G50) gives a total of 6.32 in. The total limit is 1.0 in (Specification 31 20 00 Article 3.6.A), so the utilisation is 6.32; the consolidation component alone is 5.42 times the total limit. If the 50-psf recompression band to σ'p is credited (Cr = 0.045), Sc = 5.12 in and the total is 6.02 in. If σ'0 is recomputed from the project profile (Finding 5), Sc = 5.86 in and the total is 6.76 in. The range 6.0–6.8 in is 6.0–6.8 times the limit. Because the immediate component alone is 0.90 in (90% of the limit), any positive consolidation takes the total over the limit: even at half the stated Δσ (450 psf), Sc is still 2.97 in and the total is 3.87 in. Secondary compression is not included, so 6.3 in is a lower bound on the long-term total. The GIR's own sensitivity table (Table 8-1) gives 5.9 in at q = 1,000 psf, consistent with this result.

034| Table 3 — Long-term consolidation and total settlement, computed independently from the record. All cases exceed the 1.0 in total limit.

035| Finding 3 — The calculation is not based on the current issued documents.

036| CB-GEO-007 Sheet 2 (note A36) cites "S-101 Foundation Plan Rev.2 (09/12/2025)", and the Cover cites the "Owner's Basis of Design memo (Rev.1, 06/12/2025)" as its criteria source. The current S-101 is Rev.4 dated 05/29/2026; its revision block records Rev.2 as 12/12/2025, not 09/12/2025. The current DBM is Rev.2 dated 11/14/2025, which supersedes Rev.1 dated 07/18/2025; there is no DBM Rev.1 dated 06/12/2025. The calculation is dated 09/30/2025, before both current documents. The Cover also describes Block C as "spread-footing foundations on Stratum 2 clay bearing", while Sheet 2 correctly describes isolated footings on Stratum 1 sand about 2.5 ft above the clay; the footing bears on the sand and the clay is the settlement stratum. The calculation therefore does not trace to the current revision record, and its stated criteria source is a superseded or misidentified DBM.

037| Finding 4 — The as-built footing geometry and current Sheet S-201 Rev.4 do not agree.

038| CB-GEO-007 Sheet 2 and the monitoring records (Monitoring Points sheet) describe Block C footings 8.5–10.5 ft square, 30–36 in thick, with underside El. 740.5. Sheet S-201 Rev.4 Detail 3 shows a typical interior Block C footing 7'-6" × 7'-6" × 2'-0" with underside El. 746.0. A 7.5-ft square footing at the 4,000 psf net allowable pressure can carry about 225 kips, less than the 264–432 kip service loads tabulated in CB-GEO-007 Sheet 2; it cannot be the governing as-built interior footing. The EOR must reconcile S-201 Rev.4 with the as-built/monitoring geometry and confirm the geometry used in the revised settlement analysis. The as-built/monitoring geometry matches the calculation's 8.5–10.5 ft schedule and is the geometry I treated as governing; the current drawing conflict is itself a record non-conformance.

039| Finding 5 — The adopted σ'0 = 1,850 psf is not reproducible from the profile and water table; the conclusion is unchanged.

040| At mid-clay El. 729.0, with 12 ft of upper sand at 118 pcf, 9 ft of clay at 120 pcf and the design water table at El. 742.0, the vertical total stress is σv = 12 × 118 + 9 × 120 = 2,496 psf and the pore pressure is u = (742.0 − 729.0) × 62.4 = 811 psf, giving σ'0 = 1,685 psf. GIR Rev.2 Table 5-1 and VMT Summary B14 state 1,850 psf (about 10% higher), but neither document shows the calculation; 1,850 psf is consistent with a water table near El. 739.4, not El. 742.0. Using the lower, profile-derived value increases Sc from 5.42 to 5.86 in (total 6.76 in), so the conclusion is unchanged. Kelbrook should confirm the correct σ'0 basis, and the EOR should use the confirmed value. I used the GIR value for the primary check and the profile value for the worst-case check.

041| Finding 6 — Monitoring confirms the settlement is real, ongoing and already significant.

042| Settlement Monitoring Records — Block C (SM-BLKC-2026-Rev14), Readings sheet, Round 15 (06/26/2026), records a maximum cumulative settlement of 0.61 in at MP-7 (column C-7, footing F-C7, heaviest tributary load) and a minimum of 0.31 in at MP-12; the overall range is 0.30 in. The 0.61 in is 61% of the 1.0 in total tolerance, 74% of the 0.82 in immediate settlement calculated for F-C7 (CB-GEO-007 Sheet 3 cell G44) and 68% of the 0.90 in maximum immediate settlement, before the omitted consolidation. The MP-7 rate increased from 0.03 in per 14-day interval in the first three rounds (0.0021 in/day) to 0.06–0.07 in per interval in the last three (0.0045–0.0050 in/day), a factor of about 2.1; the record states the rate is not decreasing (Cover, Observations Summary; Trend Chart). At the last-interval rate, the 1.0 in tolerance would be reached in about 78 days, around 09/12/2026; at the last-three-round average, about 86 days, around 09/20/2026. With cv ≈ 0.041 ft²/day and a 9-ft drainage path (double drainage), t90 is about 1,680 days, or 4.6 years; the 6.5-month record covers only the early part of primary consolidation. The baseline was set on 12/12/2025 after the footings were complete and backfilled, so the 0.61 in excludes pre-baseline settlement and is not the total. The groundwater record (Boring Logs and GW Monitoring, readings through 06/28/2026; Monthly Report No. 14 Section 5.4) shows the shallow and deep heads stable within El. 741.6–742.4 and El. 737.7–738.3, so drawdown is not the cause. The monitoring is consistent with a settlement process that is still developing, not with a 0.9 in total that is nearly complete: 0.61 in has already been measured, the rate is increasing, and the calculated immediate component for F-C7 is 0.82 in. It does not demonstrate that the 0.9 in immediate result is the total.

043| Finding 7 — Differential and angular-distortion checks are incomplete.

044| CB-GEO-007 Sheet 3 compares an immediate differential of 0.2 in between F-C6 and F-C12 over a 35.8-ft diagonal with the 0.5-in differential tolerance. The specification limit is 0.5 in over 30 ft (Specification 31 20 00 Article 3.6.A); a 35.8-ft diagonal is not the specified gauge length. The calculation gives 0.08 in for the 24–26 ft adjacent pairs, immediate only. It does not compute long-term differential settlement for any pair. The largest measured adjacent-pair difference within a 30-ft gauge is about 0.23 in (MP-3 to MP-7 and MP-8 to MP-12, both 26 ft), 46% of the 0.5-in differential tolerance; the overall range is 0.30 in. Both are increasing. The immediate angular distortion of 1/2,150 is below 1/500 (CB-GEO-007 Cover B25), but a long-term angular distortion is not computed. The 0.5-in differential and 1/500 checks are therefore not demonstrated.

045| Finding 8 — Bearing capacity and the monitoring benchmark pass; they do not cure the settlement failure.

046| Bearing capacity is not the governing issue. CB-GEO-007 Sheet 2 computes a maximum net bearing pressure of 3,730 psf at F-C6, below the 4,000 psf net allowable (DBM Rev.2 Section 9; S-201 Rev.4 Detail 3). The 0.9 in immediate settlement is also below 1.0 in by itself, but it consumes 90% of the total tolerance before any consolidation. The survey benchmark is stable within 0.003 ft (Monitoring Records Cover), and all 15 rounds closed within tolerance; the monitoring data are reliable. These checks pass but do not address the missing long-term component.

047| Finding 9 — The calculation is an unsealed workbook in the review set.

048| The CB-GEO-007 on file is the native Rev.0 workbook dated 09/30/2025. Its Cover states "Sealed by Gregory Nash, PE (Ohio PE) — see signed cover in issued PDF", but the signed/sealed PDF was not in the review set. This review is therefore of the Rev.0 workbook, not a verified sealed revision. The resubmission must include the sealed PDF, and the revised calculation must be sealed and signed by the EOR.

049| 5.  CONCLUSION AND RECOMMENDATION

050| Determination: NOT VERIFIED (design review). Item 051 is not verified. The settlement analysis is incomplete because long-term consolidation of the 18-ft clay was not computed. The designer's 0.9 in is immediate settlement only; the reviewer's total is 6.32 in on the report's σ'0 = 1,850 psf and 6.76 in on the profile-derived σ'0 = 1,685 psf, against a 1.0 in total limit (utilisation 6.3–6.8). The long-term differential is not computed; the largest measured adjacent-pair difference within 30 ft is about 0.23 in, 46% of the 0.5-in tolerance, and the overall range is 0.30 in. The 0.61 in reading is 61% of the total tolerance and the rate is increasing. The constructed Block C footings are therefore not verified for long-term serviceability. Item 051 remains Open.

051| Disposition recommended for the register: NOT VERIFIED — revise and resubmit. The item cannot be closed on the current CB-GEO-007 Rev.0. The revised calculation must include, at a minimum:

052| •	(a) long-term primary consolidation for each footing (or the governing footing) using GIR Rev.2 Section 8.1, plus secondary compression;

053| •	(b) immediate, primary and secondary settlement, with the per-footing Δσ and its basis;

054| •	(c) total and differential settlement over the 30-ft gauge and angular distortion;

055| •	(d) the confirmed as-built footing geometry, reconciled with S-201 Rev.4 and S-101 Rev.4;

056| •	(e) the confirmed σ'0 basis, the construction sequence and the adjacent Block B fill surcharge; and

057| •	(f) a remedial/mitigation evaluation for the constructed footings, or a demonstration that the revised analysis complies without remediation.

058| The actions required before Item 051 can be re-verified are:

059| Table 4 — Required actions, owners and timing. Item 051 stays open until the revised, sealed analysis and any required remediation are verified.

060| Schedule consequence. Item 051 cannot be closed by the 07/20/2026 due date. The earliest realistic closure is 08/07/2026, assuming the EOR resubmits the revised, sealed calculation by 07/31/2026 and Thelbridge completes its review within five business days. Remedial construction, if required, would extend beyond that. This memorandum does not release the 07/22/2026 Level-3 placement; that is the consolidated hold-point decision. Item 051 is not one of the three minimum items conditioning that hold-point in the register schedule (Items 052, 053 and 057), but under Specification 31 20 00 Article 3.6.B no additional load may be applied to Block C until a written disposition is issued; the EOR and Contractor must confirm that the Level-3 placement and its load path do not load the Block C footings before the hold-point is released.
