1.  PURPOSE
This memorandum records Thelbridge's verification review of Item 051 on the Package A Review Comment and Verification Register. Item 051 requires verification of the Block C spread-footing foundations for long-term settlement of the underlying compressible CL clay (Cc = 0.28, e0 = 0.92, σ'p = 1,900 psf; 18 ft layer) under a stress increase Δσ = 900 psf at mid-layer, against the project tolerance of 1.0 in total and 0.5 in differential, and correlation with the 0.61 in cumulative reading of 06/26/2026. The item is due 07/20/2026, two days before the 07/22/2026 Level-3 concrete placement.
The question is whether the Block C settlement analysis (CB-GEO-007) is complete and reconciled to the project tolerances, and whether the constructed footings are verified for long-term serviceability. The review covers the twelve Block C footings (C-1 through C-12) bearing in the upper sand above the CL clay aquitard from El. 738.0 to El. 720.0. It does not cover bearing capacity of the upper sand except as a cross-check, the basement mat (Item 050), the Block B piles (Item 049) or the Block B plant-room shoring (Item 048). No RFI or site instruction in the record changes the Block C settlement basis; RFI 104 concerns basement wall-to-mat joints only.
2.  DOCUMENTS REVIEWED
The review was made against the following documents, read in the revisions stated. Superseded revisions were identified and are not relied on.
Table 1 — Documents reviewed. GIR Rev.1 (12/12/2024) and DBM Rev.1 (07/18/2025) are superseded and were not used. The CB-GEO-007 signed/sealed PDF referenced on its cover was not in the review set; the native Rev.0 workbook was reviewed.
3.  BASIS OF REVIEW
The governing requirements applied are:
•	Specification 31 20 00 Rev.3, Article 3.6.A: total settlement 1.0 in maximum; differential settlement 0.5 in maximum over 30 ft.
•	Specification 31 20 00 Rev.3, Article 3.6.B: where predicted or monitored settlement exceeds either tolerance, the Structural Engineer of Record shall be notified in writing and no additional load shall be applied until a written disposition is issued.
•	Specification 31 20 00 Rev.3, Article 3.6.C: settlement readings shall be taken and transmitted to the Owner's Representative Engineer at the indicated frequency; cumulative settlement approaching either tolerance shall be reported immediately.
•	Geotechnical Investigation Report Rev.2, Section 8.1: long-term one-dimensional consolidation settlement shall be computed by Sc = Cc·H/(1+e0)·log10[(σ'0+q)/σ'0], with Cc = 0.28, e0 = 0.92, H = 18 ft and σ'0 = 1,850 psf at mid-depth (El. 729.0); σ'p = 1,900 psf (OCR 1.03), so any q above about 50 psf produces virgin compression.
•	Geotechnical Investigation Report Rev.2, Section 9.1: the Structural Engineer of Record must explicitly compute consolidation settlement of the clay under the stress increase q at mid-depth caused by each governing footing, using the Table 5-1 parameters, and reconcile the result against the total-and-differential settlement tolerances.
•	Design Basis Memorandum Rev.2, Section 7.3: Block C settlement is a serviceability check in CB-GEO-007, using the tolerances in Specification 31 20 00 Article 3.6. Section 9: the geotechnical report controls all soil parameters, and any conflict is resolved in favour of that report.
•	ASTM D2435/D2435M-11 (Reapproved 2020): one-dimensional consolidation test method used by Vantree for the clay parameters.
The register's reference tab records the 1.0 in / 0.5 in values as descriptive facts from CB-GEO-007; the controlling source is Specification 31 20 00 Rev.3 Article 3.6.A, which the DBM also cites. The inputs used in the independent recomputation are listed in Table 2. I applied the stricter reading where the record allows two readings: the 1.0 in limit is applied to total settlement (immediate plus primary plus secondary), not to immediate settlement alone; the 0.5 in differential limit is applied over a 30-ft gauge, not a longer diagonal; and both predicted and monitored settlement are treated as triggers under Article 3.6.B.
Table 2 — Inputs used in the independent recomputation, with their record source.
4.  FINDINGS
Finding 1 — CB-GEO-007 does not compute long-term consolidation; Sheet 4 is blank.
CB-GEO-007 Sheet 4 — Consolidation (rows 6 to 15) is a table of placeholders ("—"). Cell A15 states: "Not computed. Serviceability taken from the immediate settlement result on Sheet 3." The Sheet 3 conclusion (cells A69–A70) is expressly limited to "Immediate elastic settlement ... 0.9 in" and a differential of 0.2 in. The calculation therefore does not compute consolidation of the 18-ft CL clay, although GIR Rev.2 Sections 8.1 and 9.1 require the Structural Engineer of Record to compute it explicitly for each governing footing and reconcile it to the tolerances, and DBM Rev.2 Section 7.3 records that Block C settlement is checked in CB-GEO-007. The omission is the governing long-term mechanism, not a presentation gap: without it, the 0.9 in cannot be compared with the 1.0 in total limit.
Finding 2 — The recomputed long-term consolidation is 5.42 in; total settlement is 6.32 in against a 1.0 in limit.
Using the GIR's own one-dimensional equation and the parameters in Table 2:
Sc = Cc·H/(1+e0)·log10[(σ'0 + Δσ)/σ'0] = 0.28 × 18/(1 + 0.92) × log10[(1,850 + 900)/1,850]
= 2.625 × log10(1.4865) = 0.452 ft = 5.42 in.
Adding the calculated immediate settlement of 0.90 in (CB-GEO-007 Sheet 3 cell G50) gives a total of 6.32 in. The total limit is 1.0 in (Specification 31 20 00 Article 3.6.A), so the utilisation is 6.32; the consolidation component alone is 5.42 times the total limit. If the 50-psf recompression band to σ'p is credited (Cr = 0.045), Sc = 5.12 in and the total is 6.02 in. If σ'0 is recomputed from the project profile (Finding 5), Sc = 5.86 in and the total is 6.76 in. The range 6.0–6.8 in is 6.0–6.8 times the limit. Because the immediate component alone is 0.90 in (90% of the limit), any positive consolidation takes the total over the limit: even at half the stated Δσ (450 psf), Sc is still 2.97 in and the total is 3.87 in. Secondary compression is not included, so 6.3 in is a lower bound on the long-term total. The GIR's own sensitivity table (Table 8-1) gives 5.9 in at q = 1,000 psf, consistent with this result.
Table 3 — Long-term consolidation and total settlement, computed independently from the record. All cases exceed the 1.0 in total limit.
Finding 3 — The calculation is not based on the current issued documents.
CB-GEO-007 Sheet 2 (note A36) cites "S-101 Foundation Plan Rev.2 (09/12/2025)", and the Cover cites the "Owner's Basis of Design memo (Rev.1, 06/12/2025)" as its criteria source. The current S-101 is Rev.4 dated 05/29/2026; its revision block records Rev.2 as 12/12/2025, not 09/12/2025. The current DBM is Rev.2 dated 11/14/2025, which supersedes Rev.1 dated 07/18/2025; there is no DBM Rev.1 dated 06/12/2025. The calculation is dated 09/30/2025, before both current documents. The Cover also describes Block C as "spread-footing foundations on Stratum 2 clay bearing", while Sheet 2 correctly describes isolated footings on Stratum 1 sand about 2.5 ft above the clay; the footing bears on the sand and the clay is the settlement stratum. The calculation therefore does not trace to the current revision record, and its stated criteria source is a superseded or misidentified DBM.
Finding 4 — The as-built footing geometry and current Sheet S-201 Rev.4 do not agree.
CB-GEO-007 Sheet 2 gives Block C footings 8.5–10.5 ft square at underside El. 740.5; the monitoring records (Monitoring Points sheet) identify the same 8.5–10.5 ft sizes and 30–36 in thicknesses. Sheet S-201 Rev.4 Detail 3 shows a typical interior Block C footing 7'-6" × 7'-6" × 2'-0" with underside El. 746.0. A 7.5-ft square footing at the 4,000 psf net allowable pressure can carry about 225 kips, less than the 264–432 kip service loads tabulated in CB-GEO-007 Sheet 2; it cannot be the governing as-built interior footing. The EOR must reconcile S-201 Rev.4 with the as-built/monitoring geometry and confirm the geometry used in the revised settlement analysis. The as-built/monitoring geometry matches the calculation's 8.5–10.5 ft schedule and is the geometry I treated as governing; the current drawing conflict is itself a record non-conformance.
Finding 5 — The adopted σ'0 = 1,850 psf is not reproducible from the profile and water table; the conclusion is unchanged.
At mid-clay El. 729.0, with 12 ft of upper sand at 118 pcf, 9 ft of clay at 120 pcf and the design water table at El. 742.0, the vertical total stress is σv = 12 × 118 + 9 × 120 = 2,496 psf and the pore pressure is u = (742.0 − 729.0) × 62.4 = 811 psf, giving σ'0 = 1,685 psf. GIR Rev.2 Table 5-1 and VMT Summary B14 state 1,850 psf (about 10% higher), but neither document shows the calculation; 1,850 psf is consistent with a water table near El. 739.4, not El. 742.0. Using the lower, profile-derived value increases Sc from 5.42 to 5.86 in (total 6.76 in), so the conclusion is unchanged. Kelbrook should confirm the correct σ'0 basis, and the EOR should use the confirmed value. I used the GIR value for the primary check and the profile value for the worst-case check.
Finding 6 — Monitoring confirms the settlement is real, ongoing and already significant.
Settlement Monitoring Records — Block C (SM-BLKC-2026-Rev14), Readings sheet, Round 15 (06/26/2026), records a maximum cumulative settlement of 0.61 in at MP-7 (column C-7, footing F-C7, heaviest tributary load) and a minimum of 0.31 in at MP-12; the overall range is 0.30 in. The 0.61 in is 61% of the 1.0 in total tolerance, 74% of the 0.82 in immediate settlement calculated for F-C7 (CB-GEO-007 Sheet 3 cell G44) and 68% of the 0.90 in maximum immediate settlement, before the omitted consolidation. The MP-7 rate increased from 0.03 in per 14-day interval in the first three rounds (0.0021 in/day) to 0.06–0.07 in per interval in the last three (0.0045–0.0050 in/day), a factor of about 2.1; the record states the rate is not decreasing (Cover, Observations Summary; Trend Chart). At the last-interval rate, the 1.0 in tolerance would be reached in about 78 days, around 09/12/2026; at the last-three-round average, about 86 days, around 09/20/2026. With cv ≈ 0.041 ft²/day and a 9-ft drainage path (double drainage), t90 is about 1,680 days, or 4.6 years; the 6.5-month record covers only the early part of primary consolidation. The baseline was set on 12/12/2025 after the footings were complete and backfilled, so the 0.61 in excludes pre-baseline settlement and is not the total. The groundwater record (Boring Logs and GW Monitoring, readings through 06/28/2026; Monthly Report No. 14 Section 5.4) shows the shallow and deep heads stable within El. 741.6–742.4 and El. 737.7–738.3, so drawdown is not the cause. The monitoring is consistent with a settlement process that is still developing, not with a 0.9 in total that is nearly complete: 0.61 in has already been measured, the rate is increasing, and the calculated immediate component for F-C7 is 0.82 in. It does not demonstrate that the 0.9 in immediate result is the total.
Finding 7 — Differential and angular-distortion checks are incomplete.
CB-GEO-007 Sheet 3 compares an immediate differential of 0.2 in between F-C6 and F-C12 over a 35.8-ft diagonal with the 0.5-in differential tolerance. The specification limit is 0.5 in over 30 ft (Specification 31 20 00 Article 3.6.A); a 35.8-ft diagonal is not the specified gauge length. The calculation gives 0.08 in for the 24–26 ft adjacent pairs, immediate only. It does not compute long-term differential settlement for any pair. The largest measured adjacent-pair difference within a 30-ft gauge is about 0.23 in (MP-3 to MP-7 and MP-8 to MP-12, both 26 ft), 46% of the 0.5-in differential tolerance; the overall range is 0.30 in. Both are increasing. The immediate angular distortion of 1/2,150 (CB-GEO-007 Sheet 3) is below the 1/500 limit (Cover B25), but a long-term angular distortion is not computed. The 0.5-in differential and 1/500 checks are therefore not demonstrated.
Finding 8 — Bearing capacity and the monitoring benchmark pass; they do not cure the settlement failure.
Bearing capacity is not the governing issue on the as-built/calculation geometry. CB-GEO-007 Sheet 2 computes a maximum net bearing pressure of 3,730 psf at F-C6, below the 4,000 psf net allowable (DBM Rev.2 Section 9; S-201 Rev.4 Detail 3). If the 7.5-ft S-201 Rev.4 detail were the governing geometry, the footings would be under-sized in bearing as well (Finding 4). The 0.9 in immediate settlement is also below 1.0 in by itself, but it consumes 90% of the total tolerance before any consolidation. The survey benchmark is stable within 0.003 ft (Monitoring Records Cover), and all 15 rounds closed within tolerance; the monitoring data are reliable. These checks pass but do not address the missing long-term component.
Finding 9 — The calculation is an unsealed workbook in the review set.
The CB-GEO-007 on file is the native Rev.0 workbook dated 09/30/2025. Its Cover states "Sealed by Gregory Nash, PE (Ohio PE) — see signed cover in issued PDF", but the signed/sealed PDF was not in the review set. This review is therefore of the Rev.0 workbook, not a verified sealed revision. The resubmission must include the sealed PDF, and the revised calculation must be sealed and signed by the EOR.
Table 4 summarises the classification of each governing check. The detailed working is in Findings 1 to 9.
Table 4 — Classification of the governing checks. Only the bearing check on the as-built geometry and the monitoring data are valid; the settlement, differential and calculation-basis checks need revision.
5.  CONCLUSION AND RECOMMENDATION
Determination: NOT VERIFIED (design review). Item 051 is not verified. The settlement analysis is incomplete because long-term consolidation of the 18-ft clay was not computed. The designer's 0.9 in is immediate settlement only; the reviewer's total is 6.32 in on the report's σ'0 = 1,850 psf and 6.76 in on the profile-derived σ'0 = 1,685 psf, against a 1.0 in total limit (utilisation 6.3–6.8). The long-term differential is not computed; the largest measured adjacent-pair difference within 30 ft is about 0.23 in, 46% of the 0.5-in tolerance, and the overall range is 0.30 in. The 0.61 in reading is 61% of the total tolerance and the rate is increasing. The constructed Block C footings are therefore not verified for long-term serviceability. Item 051 remains Open. Under the Owner's 07/06/2026 directive, permanent work requires Thelbridge's written verification; this memorandum does not clear Item 051.
Disposition recommended for the register: NOT VERIFIED — revise and resubmit. The item cannot be closed on the current CB-GEO-007 Rev.0. The revised calculation must include, at a minimum:
•	(a) long-term primary consolidation for each footing (or the governing footing) using GIR Rev.2 Section 8.1, plus secondary compression;
•	(b) immediate, primary and secondary settlement, with the per-footing Δσ and its basis;
•	(c) total and differential settlement over the 30-ft gauge and angular distortion;
•	(d) the confirmed as-built footing geometry, reconciled with S-201 Rev.4 and S-101 Rev.4;
•	(e) the confirmed σ'0 basis, the construction sequence and the adjacent Block B fill surcharge; and
•	(f) a remedial/mitigation evaluation for the constructed footings, or a demonstration that the revised analysis complies without remediation.
The actions required before Item 051 can be re-verified are:
Table 5 — Required actions, owners and timing. Item 051 stays open until the revised, sealed analysis and any required remediation are verified.
Schedule consequence. Item 051 cannot close by 07/20/2026. Earliest realistic closure is 08/07/2026, assuming the EOR resubmits the revised, sealed calculation by 07/31/2026 and Thelbridge reviews it within five business days; remediation, if required, extends beyond. This memorandum does not release the 07/22/2026 Level-3 placement. Item 051 is not one of the three minimum hold-point items (052, 053, 057), but under Specification 31 20 00 Article 3.6.B no additional load may be applied to Block C until written disposition; the EOR and Contractor must confirm the Level-3 placement and load path do not load Block C before the hold-point is released.

THELBRIDGE PROJECT MANAGEMENT SERVICES
500 South High Street, Suite 720, Columbus, OH 43215  |  (614) 555-0125  |  thelbridgepm.com
VERIFICATION MEMORANDUM
To:	Adrian Vance, Project Engineer (Structural/Geotechnical), Owner's Representative
From:	Rahul Nimkar, Geotechnical Reviewer
Date:	07/20/2026
Subject:	Item 051 — Block C Spread Footings — Long-Term Settlement Verification, Package A
cc:	Rachel Marlbeck, University Program Director, Thornbury State University
Determination: NOT VERIFIED (design review). Item 051 remains Open. The settlement analysis omits long-term consolidation and checks only 12 representative footings; the computed total is 6.3–6.8 in against a 1.0 in limit. Revise and resubmit.
1.  PURPOSE
This memorandum records Thelbridge's verification review of Item 051 on the Package A Review Comment and Verification Register. Item 051 requires verification of the Block C spread-footing foundations for long-term settlement of the underlying compressible CL clay (Cc = 0.28, e0 = 0.92, σ'p = 1,900 psf; 18 ft layer) under a stress increase Δσ = 900 psf at mid-layer, against the project tolerance of 1.0 in total and 0.5 in differential, and correlation with the 0.61 in cumulative reading of 06/26/2026. The item is due 07/20/2026, two days before the 07/22/2026 Level-3 concrete placement.
The question is whether the Block C settlement analysis (CB-GEO-007) is complete and reconciled to the project tolerances, and whether the constructed footings are verified for long-term serviceability. The review covers the twelve footings in the CB-GEO-007 schedule (F-C1 through F-C12) bearing in the upper sand above the CL clay aquitard from El. 738.0 to El. 720.0; whether that schedule covers the full Block C footing population shown on S-101 Rev.4 is addressed in Finding 1. It does not cover bearing capacity of the upper sand except as a cross-check, the basement mat (Item 050), the Block B piles (Item 049) or the Block B plant-room shoring (Item 048). No RFI or site instruction in the record changes the Block C settlement basis; RFI 104 concerns basement wall-to-mat joints only.
2.  DOCUMENTS REVIEWED
The review was made against the following documents, read in the revisions stated. Superseded revisions were identified and are not relied on.
Table 1 — Documents reviewed. GIR Rev.1 (12/12/2024) and DBM Rev.1 (07/18/2025) are superseded and were not used. The CB-GEO-007 signed/sealed PDF referenced on its cover was not in the review set; the native Rev.0 workbook was reviewed.
3.  BASIS OF REVIEW
The governing requirements applied are:
•	Specification 31 20 00 Rev.3, Article 3.6.A: total settlement 1.0 in maximum; differential settlement 0.5 in maximum over 30 ft.
•	Specification 31 20 00 Rev.3, Article 3.6.B: where predicted or monitored settlement exceeds either tolerance, the Structural Engineer of Record shall be notified in writing and no additional load shall be applied until a written disposition is issued.
•	Specification 31 20 00 Rev.3, Article 3.6.C: settlement readings shall be taken and transmitted to the Owner's Representative Engineer at the indicated frequency; cumulative settlement approaching either tolerance shall be reported immediately.
•	Geotechnical Investigation Report Rev.2, Section 8.1: long-term one-dimensional consolidation settlement shall be computed by Sc = Cc·H/(1+e0)·log10[(σ'0+q)/σ'0], with Cc = 0.28, e0 = 0.92, H = 18 ft and σ'0 = 1,850 psf at mid-depth (El. 729.0); σ'p = 1,900 psf (OCR 1.03), so any q above about 50 psf produces virgin compression.
•	Geotechnical Investigation Report Rev.2, Section 9.1: the Structural Engineer of Record must explicitly compute consolidation settlement of the clay under the stress increase q at mid-depth caused by each governing footing, using the Table 5-1 parameters, and reconcile the result against the total-and-differential settlement tolerances.
•	Design Basis Memorandum Rev.2, Section 7.3: Block C settlement is a serviceability check in CB-GEO-007, using the tolerances in Specification 31 20 00 Article 3.6. Section 9: the geotechnical report controls all soil parameters, and any conflict is resolved in favour of that report.
•	ASTM D2435/D2435M-11 (Reapproved 2020): one-dimensional consolidation test method used by Vantree for the clay parameters.
The register's reference tab records the 1.0 in / 0.5 in values as descriptive facts from CB-GEO-007; the controlling source is Specification 31 20 00 Rev.3 Article 3.6.A, which the DBM also cites. The inputs used in the independent recomputation are listed in Table 2. I applied the stricter reading where the record allows two readings: the 1.0 in limit is applied to total settlement (immediate plus primary plus secondary), not to immediate settlement alone; the 0.5 in differential limit is applied over a 30-ft gauge, not a longer diagonal; and both predicted and monitored settlement are treated as triggers under Article 3.6.B.
Table 2 — Inputs used in the independent recomputation, with their record source.
4.  FINDINGS
Finding 1 — CB-GEO-007 does not compute long-term consolidation and checks only 12 representative footings.
CB-GEO-007 Sheet 4 — Consolidation (rows 6 to 15) is a table of placeholders ("—"). Cell A15 states: "Not computed. Serviceability taken from the immediate settlement result on Sheet 3." The Sheet 3 conclusion (cells A69–A70) is expressly limited to "Immediate elastic settlement ... 0.9 in" and a differential of 0.2 in. The calculation therefore does not compute consolidation of the 18-ft CL clay, although GIR Rev.2 Sections 8.1 and 9.1 require the Structural Engineer of Record to compute it explicitly for each governing footing and reconcile it to the tolerances, and DBM Rev.2 Section 7.3 records that Block C settlement is checked in CB-GEO-007. The omission is the governing long-term mechanism, not a presentation gap: without it, the 0.9 in cannot be compared with the 1.0 in total limit.
The footing schedule is also incomplete. CB-GEO-007 Sheet 2 is expressly a "representative columns" schedule of 12 footings (F-C1 through F-C12; Sheet 2, rows 18–31). S-101 Rev.4 identifies the Block C column grid as B–L / 6–8 (30 grid intersections) and shows spread-footing symbols across that grid; the plan contains substantially more than 12 footings. The calculation does not demonstrate that the 12 are the governing worst-case set or that the remaining footings were checked, although GIR Rev.2 Section 9.1 requires each governing footing. The 12-point monitoring array matches the 12 calculated footings, so the unmonitored footings have no settlement record. This is a second, independent completeness gap.
Finding 2 — The recomputed long-term consolidation is 5.42 in; total settlement is 6.32 in against a 1.0 in limit.
Using the GIR's own one-dimensional equation and the parameters in Table 2:
Sc = Cc·H/(1+e0)·log10[(σ'0 + Δσ)/σ'0] = 0.28 × 18/(1 + 0.92) × log10[(1,850 + 900)/1,850]
= 2.625 × log10(1.4865) = 0.452 ft = 5.42 in.
Adding the calculated immediate settlement of 0.90 in (CB-GEO-007 Sheet 3 cell G50) gives a total of 6.32 in. The total limit is 1.0 in (Specification 31 20 00 Article 3.6.A), so the utilisation is 6.32; the consolidation component alone is 5.42 times the total limit. If the 50-psf recompression band to σ'p is credited (Cr = 0.045), Sc = 5.12 in and the total is 6.02 in. If σ'0 is recomputed from the project profile (Finding 5), Sc = 5.86 in and the total is 6.76 in. The range 6.0–6.8 in is 6.0–6.8 times the limit. Because the immediate component alone is 0.90 in (90% of the limit), any positive consolidation takes the total over the limit: even at half the stated Δσ (450 psf), Sc is still 2.97 in and the total is 3.87 in. Secondary compression is not included, so 6.3 in is a lower bound on the long-term total. The GIR's own sensitivity table (Table 8-1) gives 5.9 in at q = 1,000 psf, consistent with this result.
Table 3 — Long-term consolidation and total settlement, computed independently from the record. All cases exceed the 1.0 in total limit.
Finding 3 — The calculation is not based on the current issued documents.
CB-GEO-007 Sheet 2 (note A36) cites "S-101 Foundation Plan Rev.2 (09/12/2025)", and the Cover cites the "Owner's Basis of Design memo (Rev.1, 06/12/2025)" as its criteria source. The current S-101 is Rev.4 dated 05/29/2026; its revision block records Rev.2 as 12/12/2025, not 09/12/2025. The current DBM is Rev.2 dated 11/14/2025, which supersedes Rev.1 dated 07/18/2025; there is no DBM Rev.1 dated 06/12/2025. The calculation is dated 09/30/2025, before both current documents. The Cover also describes Block C as "spread-footing foundations on Stratum 2 clay bearing", while Sheet 2 correctly describes isolated footings on Stratum 1 sand about 2.5 ft above the clay; the footing bears on the sand and the clay is the settlement stratum. The calculation therefore does not trace to the current revision record, and its stated criteria source is a superseded or misidentified DBM.
Finding 4 — The as-built footing geometry and current Sheet S-201 Rev.4 do not agree.
CB-GEO-007 Sheet 2 gives Block C footings 8.5–10.5 ft square at underside El. 740.5; the monitoring records (Monitoring Points sheet) identify the same 8.5–10.5 ft sizes and 30–36 in thicknesses. Sheet S-201 Rev.4 Detail 3 shows a typical interior Block C footing 7'-6" × 7'-6" × 2'-0" with underside El. 746.0. A 7.5-ft square footing at the 4,000 psf net allowable pressure can carry about 225 kips, less than the 264–432 kip service loads tabulated in CB-GEO-007 Sheet 2; it cannot be the governing as-built footing for the tabulated Block C columns. The EOR must reconcile S-201 Rev.4 with the as-built/monitoring geometry and confirm the geometry used in the revised settlement analysis. The as-built/monitoring geometry matches the calculation's 8.5–10.5 ft schedule and is the geometry I treated as governing; the current drawing conflict is itself a record non-conformance.
Finding 5 — The adopted σ'0 = 1,850 psf is not reproducible from the profile and water table; the conclusion is unchanged.
At mid-clay El. 729.0, with 12 ft of upper sand at 118 pcf, 9 ft of clay at 120 pcf and the design water table at El. 742.0, the vertical total stress is σv = 12 × 118 + 9 × 120 = 2,496 psf and the pore pressure is u = (742.0 − 729.0) × 62.4 = 811 psf, giving σ'0 = 1,685 psf. GIR Rev.2 Table 5-1 and VMT Summary B14 state 1,850 psf (about 10% higher), but neither document shows the calculation; 1,850 psf is consistent with a water table near El. 739.4, not El. 742.0. Using the lower, profile-derived value increases Sc from 5.42 to 5.86 in (total 6.76 in), so the conclusion is unchanged. Kelbrook should confirm the correct σ'0 basis, and the EOR should use the confirmed value. I used the GIR value for the primary check and the profile value for the worst-case check.
Finding 6 — Monitoring confirms the settlement is real, ongoing and already significant.
Settlement Monitoring Records — Block C (SM-BLKC-2026-Rev14), Readings sheet, Round 15 (06/26/2026), records a maximum cumulative settlement of 0.61 in at MP-7 (column C-7, footing F-C7, heaviest tributary load) and a minimum of 0.31 in at MP-12; the overall range is 0.30 in. The 0.61 in is 61% of the 1.0 in total tolerance, 74% of the 0.82 in immediate settlement calculated for F-C7 (CB-GEO-007 Sheet 3 cell G44) and 68% of the 0.90 in maximum immediate settlement, before the omitted consolidation. The MP-7 rate increased from 0.03 in per 14-day interval in the first three rounds (0.0021 in/day) to 0.06–0.07 in per interval in the last three (0.0045–0.0050 in/day), a factor of about 2.1; the record states the rate is not decreasing (Cover, Observations Summary; Trend Chart). At the last-interval rate, the 1.0 in tolerance would be reached in about 78 days, around 09/12/2026; at the last-three-round average, about 86 days, around 09/20/2026. With cv ≈ 0.041 ft²/day and a 9-ft drainage path (double drainage), t90 is about 1,680 days, or 4.6 years; the 6.5-month record covers only the early part of primary consolidation. The baseline was set on 12/12/2025 after the footings were complete and backfilled, so the 0.61 in excludes pre-baseline settlement and is not the total. The groundwater record (Boring Logs and GW Monitoring, readings through 06/28/2026; Monthly Report No. 14 Section 5.4) shows the shallow and deep heads stable within El. 741.6–742.4 and El. 737.7–738.3, so drawdown is not the cause. The monitoring is consistent with a settlement process that is still developing, not with a 0.9 in total that is nearly complete: 0.61 in has already been measured, the rate is increasing, and the calculated immediate component for F-C7 is 0.82 in. It does not demonstrate that the 0.9 in immediate result is the total.
Finding 7 — Differential and angular-distortion checks are incomplete.
CB-GEO-007 Sheet 3 compares an immediate differential of 0.2 in between F-C6 and F-C12 over a 35.8-ft diagonal with the 0.5-in differential tolerance. The specification limit is 0.5 in over 30 ft (Specification 31 20 00 Article 3.6.A); a 35.8-ft diagonal is not the specified gauge length. The calculation gives 0.08 in for the 24–26 ft adjacent pairs, immediate only. It does not compute long-term differential settlement for any pair. The largest measured adjacent-pair difference within a 30-ft gauge is about 0.23 in (MP-3 to MP-7 and MP-8 to MP-12, both 26 ft), 46% of the 0.5-in differential tolerance; the overall range is 0.30 in. Both are increasing. The immediate angular distortion of 1/2,150 (CB-GEO-007 Sheet 3) is below the 1/500 limit (Cover B25), but a long-term angular distortion is not computed. The 0.5-in differential and 1/500 checks are therefore not demonstrated.
Finding 8 — Bearing capacity and the monitoring benchmark pass; they do not cure the settlement failure.
Bearing capacity is not the governing issue on the as-built/calculation geometry. CB-GEO-007 Sheet 2 computes a maximum net bearing pressure of 3,730 psf at F-C6, below the 4,000 psf net allowable (DBM Rev.2 Section 9; S-201 Rev.4 Detail 3). If the 7.5-ft S-201 Rev.4 detail were the governing geometry, the footings would be under-sized in bearing as well (Finding 4). The 0.9 in immediate settlement is also below 1.0 in by itself, but it consumes 90% of the total tolerance before any consolidation. The survey benchmark is stable within 0.003 ft (Monitoring Records Cover), and all 15 rounds closed within tolerance; the monitoring data are reliable. These checks pass but do not address the missing long-term component.
Finding 9 — The calculation is an unsealed workbook in the review set.
The CB-GEO-007 on file is the native Rev.0 workbook dated 09/30/2025. Its Cover states "Sealed by Gregory Nash, PE (Ohio PE) — see signed cover in issued PDF", but the signed/sealed PDF was not in the review set. This review is therefore of the Rev.0 workbook, not a verified sealed revision. The resubmission must include the sealed PDF, and the revised calculation must be sealed and signed by the EOR.
Table 4 summarises the classification of the principal governing checks. The detailed working is in Findings 1 to 9.
Table 4 — Classification of the governing checks. Only the bearing check on the as-built geometry and the monitoring data are valid; the settlement, coverage, differential and angular checks need revision.
5.  CONCLUSION AND RECOMMENDATION
Determination: NOT VERIFIED (design review). Item 051 is not verified. The settlement analysis is incomplete because long-term consolidation of the 18-ft clay was not computed, and the calculation checks only 12 representative footings rather than the full S-101 Rev.4 population. The designer's 0.9 in is immediate settlement only; the reviewer's total is 6.32 in on the report's σ'0 = 1,850 psf and 6.76 in on the profile-derived σ'0 = 1,685 psf, against a 1.0 in total limit (utilisation 6.3–6.8). The long-term differential is not computed; the largest measured adjacent-pair difference within 30 ft is about 0.23 in, 46% of the 0.5-in tolerance, and the overall range is 0.30 in. [P][?] 4.  FINDINGS
[P][?] Finding 1 — CB-GEO-007 does not compute long-term consolidation and checks only 12 representative footings.
[P][?] CB-GEO-007 Sheet 4 — Consolidation (rows 6 to 15) is a table of placeholders ("—"). Cell A15 states: "Not computed. Serviceability taken from the immediate settlement result on Sheet 3." The Sheet 3 conclusion (cells A69–A70) is expressly limited to "Immediate elastic settlement ... 0.9 in" and a differential of 0.2 in. The calculation therefore does not compute consolidation of the 18-ft CL clay, although GIR Rev.2 Sections 8.1 and 9.1 require the Structural Engineer of Record to compute it explicitly for each governing footing and reconcile it to the tolerances, and DBM Rev.2 Section 7.3 records that Block C settlement is checked in CB-GEO-007. The omission is the governing long-term mechanism, not a presentation gap: without it, the 0.9 in cannot be compared with the 1.0 in total limit.
[P][?] The footing schedule is also incomplete. CB-GEO-007 Sheet 2 is expressly a "representative columns" schedule of 12 footings (F-C1 through F-C12; Sheet 2, rows 18–31). S-101 Rev.4 identifies the Block C column grid as B–L / 6–8 (30 grid intersections) and shows spread-footing symbols across that grid; the plan contains substantially more than 12 footings. The calculation does not demonstrate that the 12 are the governing worst-case set or that the remaining footings were checked, although GIR Rev.2 Section 9.1 requires each governing footing. The 12-point monitoring array matches the 12 calculated footings, so the unmonitored footings have no settlement record. This is a second, independent completeness gap.
[P][?] Finding 2 — The recomputed long-term consolidation is 5.42 in; total settlement is 6.32 in against a 1.0 in limit.
[P][?] Using the GIR's own one-dimensional equation and the parameters in Table 2:
[P][?] Sc = Cc·H/(1+e0)·log10[(σ'0 + Δσ)/σ'0] = 0.28 × 18/(1 + 0.92) × log10[(1,850 + 900)/1,850]
[P][?] = 2.625 × log10(1.4865) = 0.452 ft = 5.42 in.
[P][?] Adding the calculated immediate settlement of 0.90 in (CB-GEO-007 Sheet 3 cell G50) gives a total of 6.32 in. The total limit is 1.0 in (Specification 31 20 00 Article 3.6.A), so the utilisation is 6.32; the consolidation component alone is 5.42 times the total limit. If the 50-psf recompression band to σ'p is credited (Cr = 0.045), Sc = 5.12 in and the total is 6.02 in. If σ'0 is recomputed from the project profile (Finding 5), Sc = 5.86 in and the total is 6.76 in. The range 6.0–6.8 in is 6.0–6.8 times the limit. Because the immediate component alone is 0.90 in (90% of the limit), any positive consolidation takes the total over the limit: even at half the stated Δσ (450 psf), Sc is still 2.97 in and the total is 3.87 in. Secondary compression is not included, so 6.3 in is a lower bound on the long-term total. The GIR's own sensitivity table (Table 8-1) gives 5.9 in at q = 1,000 psf, consistent with this result.

[P][?] Finding 3 — The calculation is not based on the current issued documents.
[P][?] CB-GEO-007 Sheet 2 (note A36) cites "S-101 Foundation Plan Rev.2 (09/12/2025)", and the Cover cites the "Owner's Basis of Design memo (Rev.1, 06/12/2025)" as its criteria source. The current S-101 is Rev.4 dated 05/29/2026; its revision block records Rev.2 as 12/12/2025, not 09/12/2025. The current DBM is Rev.2 dated 11/14/2025, which supersedes Rev.1 dated 07/18/2025; there is no DBM Rev.1 dated 06/12/2025. The calculation is dated 09/30/2025, before both current documents. The Cover also describes Block C as "spread-footing foundations on Stratum 2 clay bearing", while Sheet 2 correctly describes isolated footings on Stratum 1 sand about 2.5 ft above the clay; the footing bears on the sand and the clay is the settlement stratum. The calculation therefore does not trace to the current revision record, and its stated criteria source is a superseded or misidentified DBM.
[P][?] Finding 4 — The as-built footing geometry and current Sheet S-201 Rev.4 do not agree.
[P][?] CB-GEO-007 Sheet 2 gives Block C footings 8.5–10.5 ft square at underside El. 740.5; the monitoring records (Monitoring Points sheet) identify the same 8.5–10.5 ft sizes and 30–36 in thicknesses. Sheet S-201 Rev.4 Detail 3 shows a typical interior Block C footing 7'-6" × 7'-6" × 2'-0" with underside El. 746.0. A 7.5-ft square footing at the 4,000 psf net allowable pressure can carry about 225 kips, less than the 264–432 kip service loads tabulated in CB-GEO-007 Sheet 2; it cannot be the governing as-built footing for the tabulated Block C columns. The EOR must reconcile S-201 Rev.4 with the as-built/monitoring geometry and confirm the geometry used in the revised settlement analysis. The monitoring geometry matches the calculation's 8.5–10.5 ft plan sizes; I treated that plan geometry as governing, but the as-built underside elevation is not confirmed by the monitoring record and must be established by the EOR. The current drawing conflict is itself a record non-conformance.
[P][?] Finding 5 — The adopted σ'0 = 1,850 psf is not reproducible from the profile and water table; the conclusion is unchanged.
[P][?] At mid-clay El. 729.0, with 12 ft of upper sand at 118 pcf, 9 ft of clay at 120 pcf and the design water table at El. 742.0, the vertical total stress is σv = 12 × 118 + 9 × 120 = 2,496 psf and the pore pressure is u = (742.0 − 729.0) × 62.4 = 811 psf, giving σ'0 = 1,685 psf. GIR Rev.2 Table 5-1 and VMT Summary B14 state 1,850 psf (about 10% higher), but neither document shows the calculation; 1,850 psf is consistent with a water table near El. 739.4, not El. 742.0. Using the lower, profile-derived value increases Sc from 5.42 to 5.86 in (total 6.76 in), so the conclusion is unchanged. Kelbrook should confirm the correct σ'0 basis, and the EOR should use the confirmed value. I used the GIR value for the primary check and the profile value for the worst-case check.
[P][?] Finding 6 — Monitoring confirms the settlement is real, ongoing and already significant.
[P][?] Settlement Monitoring Records — Block C (SM-BLKC-2026-Rev14), Readings sheet, Round 15 (06/26/2026), records a maximum cumulative settlement of 0.61 in at MP-7 (column C-7, footing F-C7, heaviest tributary load) and a minimum of 0.31 in at MP-12; the overall range is 0.30 in. The 0.61 in is 61% of the 1.0 in total tolerance, 74% of the 0.82 in immediate settlement calculated for F-C7 (CB-GEO-007 Sheet 3 cell G44) and 68% of the 0.90 in maximum immediate settlement, before the omitted consolidation. The MP-7 rate increased from 0.03 in per 14-day interval in the first three rounds (0.0021 in/day) to 0.06–0.07 in per interval in the last three (0.0045–0.0050 in/day), a factor of about 2.1; the record states the rate is not decreasing (Cover, Observations Summary; Trend Chart). At the last-interval rate, the 1.0 in tolerance would be reached in about 78 days, around 09/12/2026; at the last-three-round average, about 86 days, around 09/20/2026. With cv ≈ 0.041 ft²/day and a 9-ft drainage path (double drainage), t90 is about 1,680 days, or 4.6 years; the 6.5-month record covers only the early part of primary consolidation. The baseline was set on 12/12/2025 after the footings were complete and backfilled, so the 0.61 in excludes pre-baseline settlement and is not the total. The groundwater record (Boring Logs and GW Monitoring, readings through 06/28/2026; Monthly Report No. 14 Section 5.4) shows the shallow and deep heads stable within El. 741.6–742.4 and El. 737.7–738.3, so drawdown is not the cause. The monitoring is consistent with a settlement process that is still developing, not with a 0.9 in total that is nearly complete: 0.61 in has already been measured, the rate is increasing, and the calculated immediate component for F-C7 is 0.82 in. It does not demonstrate that the 0.9 in immediate result is the total.
[P][?] Finding 7 — Differential and angular-distortion checks are incomplete.
[P][?] CB-GEO-007 Sheet 3 compares an immediate differential of 0.2 in between F-C6 and F-C12 over a 35.8-ft diagonal with the 0.5-in differential tolerance. The specification limit is 0.5 in over 30 ft (Specification 31 20 00 Article 3.6.A); a 35.8-ft diagonal is not the specified gauge length. The calculation gives 0.08 in for the 24–26 ft adjacent pairs, immediate only. It does not compute long-term differential settlement for any pair. The largest measured adjacent-pair difference within a 30-ft gauge is about 0.23 in (MP-3 to MP-7 and MP-8 to MP-12, both 26 ft), 46% of the 0.5-in differential tolerance; the overall range is 0.30 in. Both are increasing. The immediate angular distortion of 1/2,150 (CB-GEO-007 Sheet 3) is below the 1/500 limit (Cover B25), but a long-term angular distortion is not computed. The 0.5-in differential and 1/500 checks are therefore not demonstrated.

[P][?] Bearing capacity is not the governing issue on the as-built/calculation geometry. 1.  EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
Kelbrook Geotechnical, Inc. has completed a subsurface investigation and geotechnical engineering analysis for
Package A of the Birchwood Village Expansion Program at 1802 Larchwood Avenue, Columbus, Ohio.
Package A comprises three student-housing blocks (Blocks A, B and C) constructed over a shared podium, with
a single basement level beneath Blocks A and B, and a separate deep plant-room excavation planned beneath
Block B.
The finished design grade across Package A is established at El. 750.0 ft. Existing ground surface stands at
approximately El. 750.0 across the footprints of Blocks A and C but falls to about El. 738.0 across the Block B
footprint (a former surface drainage swale). Placement of engineered fill of variable thickness — up to
approximately 12 ft beneath Block B — will therefore be required to bring the site to design grade.
The subsurface profile consists of three principal strata:
•  Stratum 1 — Upper sand, classified SP-SM (poorly-graded sand with silt), medium-dense, from
existing grade down to El. 738.0, total unit weight 118 pcf.
•  Stratum 2 — Compressible clay aquitard, classified CL (lean clay of medium plasticity),
normally-consolidated, from El. 738.0 down to El. 720.0 (18 ft thick), total unit weight 120 pcf, low
permeability. This is the strata governing settlement of shallow foundations and provides the aquitard
between the shallow and deep groundwater regimes.
•  Stratum 3 — Dense sand and gravel aquifer, classified SW-GW, below El. 720.0, total unit weight 130
pcf, confined by the overlying clay.
Groundwater is present as two distinct regimes:
•  The design water table in the upper sand is set at El. 742.0 ft. Piezometer readings taken from three
shallow standpipes over the 11/2024–02/2025 monitoring period range from El. 741.6 to El. 742.4;
groundwater seepage was observed at El. 741.8 to El. 742.2 in the Block A test-pit excavation.
•  A confined piezometric head of El. 738.0 ft has been measured in the deep sand-and-gravel aquifer
through two deep piezometers screened below El. 720.0, with readings ranging El. 737.7 to El. 738.3. The
confined head is at essentially the same elevation as the top of the clay aquitard.
Consolidation testing on two undisturbed Shelby-tube samples of the compressible clay (samples B-06 U3 and
B-08 U2, tested per ASTM D2435) yielded a compression index Cc = 0.28, a recompression index Cr = 0.045,
an initial void ratio e0 = 0.92, an in-situ vertical effective stress σ'0 = 1,850 psf, and a preconsolidation pressure
σ'p = 1,900 psf. The margin (σ'p − σ'0 ≈ 50 psf) confirms the clay is essentially normally-consolidated: any net
stress increase applied at the top of the clay will produce virgin (Cc) compression rather than recompression
(Cr) compression.
Principal geotechnical recommendations are as follows:
1.  Block C — Spread footings may be founded within the upper sand. Consolidation of the underlying
compressible clay under column-load stress increases at mid-depth of the clay must be explicitly computed
by the Structural Engineer of Record, using the parameters provided herein, and reconciled against the
settlement tolerances specified in the project structural criteria.
2.  Blocks A and B basement mat — A conventional reinforced-concrete mat foundation may be founded
within the upper sand at the design underside elevation. Hydrostatic uplift from the El. 742.0 water table
must be resolved by mat self-weight, superimposed permanent loads and, where necessary, tension
elements. The waterproofing system for the below-grade envelope must be selected for the applicable

3.  SITE DESCRIPTION AND GEOLOGIC SETTING
3.1  Site Location and Topography
The Package A site is located at 1802 Larchwood Avenue, on the western portion of the Thornbury State
University main campus in Columbus, Ohio. The site is bounded to the north by Larchwood Avenue, to the east
by an existing campus surface parking lot, to the south by an unimproved landscaped strip and to the west by an
existing academic building. The overall Package A footprint is approximately 3.7 acres.
Existing topography varies substantially across 
 Ground surface stands at approximately El. 750.0 ft
across the footprints of Blocks A and C in the northern and eastern portions of 
 Toward the southwest,
across the footprint of Block B, ground surface falls to about El. 738.0 ft (a difference of about 12 ft) in what
appears from historical aerial photography to have been a surface drainage swale draining the pre-development
ground westward toward a former off-site low area. The transition between the two elevations is gradual across
a nominal 60 to 80 ft width. Existing ground within Block B is generally covered with a thin (~0.5 to 1 ft)
mantle of soft organic-rich silty topsoil overlying the SP-SM upper sand; no fill of engineering significance is
present beneath Block B in its current condition.
3.2  Regional and Local Geology
Columbus, Ohio lies within the Till Plains section of the Central Lowland physiographic province. Regional
surficial geology is dominated by Wisconsinan-age glacial deposits — chiefly clay-rich till, glaciolacustrine silt
and clay, and outwash sand and gravel — overlying Devonian-age carbonate and shale bedrock. Local
hydrogeology is characterized by a shallow phreatic surface within the outwash and reworked outwash sands, a
laterally continuous fine-grained aquitard, and a lower confined aquifer within basal outwash sand and gravel
above bedrock.
The subsurface conditions encountered in the Package A borings are consistent with this regional framework: a
medium-dense reworked outwash sand at the surface, a low-permeability clay of glaciolacustrine origin at
intermediate depth, and a dense outwash sand and gravel aquifer at depth. Bedrock was not encountered within
the maximum boring depth of 90 ft (approximately El. 660.0). Blow counts in the SW-GW below El. 720.0
were consistently in the range N ≥ 50 blows per 6 inches, indicating a very dense sand-and-gravel deposit
suitable as a pile-bearing stratum.
3.3  Site History and Prior Use
Site historical review — including review of Franklin County parcel records, USGS topographic maps (1955
and later editions), and Thornbury State University campus master planning archives — indicates that the
Package A parcel was in agricultural use through approximately 1958, was acquired by the University in 1962,
and has been used for surface parking and landscape maintenance since. No prior structures of consequence, no
known below-grade utilities (other than a single abandoned 6-inch clay drain traced along the historic swale in
Block B), and no known industrial fill are present within the footprint. Because there is essentially no prior fill
of engineering significance, the Block B footprint requires new engineered fill — placed on the natural
clay-upper-sand contact after removal of the topsoil mantle — to bring the site to design grade.

SECTION 31 20 00
EARTH MOVING
Birchwood Village Expansion Program — Package A
Thornbury State University
Structural Engineer of Record: Calloway Braddock Structural Engineers, LLC
812 East Broad Street, Columbus, OH 43205
Revision: Rev.3  |  Issue Date: 03/06/2026  |  Supersedes: Rev.2 (issued 11/14/2025)
PART 1    GENERAL
1.1   SUMMARY
A.   Section Includes:
1.   Excavation, subgrade preparation, and grading for building foundations, mat foundations,
pile caps, footings, and slabs-on-grade within the Package A limits of work.
2.   Placement, moisture-conditioning, and compaction of engineered structural fill under
building foundations and slabs-on-grade.
3.   Backfill against foundation walls and around subsurface structures.
4.   Field quality control by the Owner's independent testing laboratory.
B.   Related Sections:
1.   Section 31 23 33 — Trenching and Backfilling for utility trenches within the building
envelope.
2.   Section 31 50 00 — Excavation Support and Protection for delegated shoring design.
3.   Section 03 30 00 — Cast-in-Place Concrete for placement of concrete against completed
subgrade.
1.2   REFERENCES
A.   Referenced Standards. The following standards are incorporated by reference to the extent
cited herein. The latest edition in effect at the date of Contract award shall govern.
1.   ASTM D698 — Standard Test Methods for Laboratory Compaction Characteristics of
Soil Using Standard Effort (Standard Proctor). Cited for historical borrow characterization
only; not the acceptance basis for Package A structural fill.
2.   ASTM D1557 — Standard Test Methods for Laboratory Compaction Characteristics of
Soil Using Modified Effort (Modified Proctor). Governing laboratory reference for
Package A structural fill.
3.   ASTM D6938 — Standard Test Methods for In-Place Density and Water Content of Soil
and Soil-Aggregate by Nuclear Methods (Shallow Depth). Governing field density test
method.
4.   ASTM D2216 — Standard Test Methods for Laboratory Determination of Water
(Moisture) Content of Soil and Rock by Mass. Referee method for moisture content
31 20 00 - Page 1 of 6
Earth Moving


--- page 2 ---
when the nuclear gauge reading is disputed.
5.   ASTM D2937 — Standard Test Method for Density of Soil in Place by the Drive-Cylinder
Method. Alternate field density method where permitted in writing by the Structural
Engineer of Record.
1.3   DEFINITIONS
A.   Structural Fill: Imported or on-site engineered soil placed and compacted in controlled lifts
beneath building foundations, mat foundations, pile caps, footings, or slabs-on-grade, and
meeting the material, gradation, and compaction requirements of this Section.
B.   Common Fill: Non-structural earth used only for site grading outside the building envelope.
C.   Lift: A single layer of loose fill placed in preparation for compaction, not exceeding the
maximum loose lift thickness specified in Part 3.
D.   Test Location: A single field-density test point at which both dry density and moisture
content are measured for compliance evaluation.
E.   Placed Material: The specific soil material actually placed in the field at the test location,
whose laboratory maximum dry density and optimum moisture content have been established
by ASTM D1557 Method C laboratory testing prior to placement, as required by Article 2.1.
1.4   QUALITY ASSURANCE
A.   Testing Laboratory. Field and laboratory testing under this Section shall be performed by the
Owner's independent construction materials testing laboratory (the “Laboratory”), contracted
directly to the Owner. The Contractor shall coordinate access, sampling opportunity, and
lift-by-lift notification with the Laboratory.
B.   Personnel. Nuclear-gauge operators shall hold current radiation safety training and shall be
documented as competent in ASTM D6938 direct-transmission procedures. Nuclear gauges
shall be calibrated within the manufacturer's stated interval and standard-count checked at
the start of each testing day.
C.   Placed-Material Correspondence. The laboratory maximum dry density and optimum
moisture content used as the acceptance denominators for any test location shall be those
determined by ASTM D1557 Method C on the material actually placed at that location. Where
the placed material differs materially from the previously characterized borrow, a new ASTM
D1557 Method C test shall be performed on the new material before further fill placement is
accepted.
1.5   SUBMITTALS
A.   Prior to structural fill placement, submit for review:
1.   Source identification for each proposed borrow, including gradation (sieve analysis),
Atterberg limits, and USCS classification.
2.   Laboratory report of maximum dry density and optimum moisture content per ASTM
D1557 Method C for each proposed source material.
3.   Placement and compaction plan identifying lift thickness, compaction equipment, and
passes.
B.   During placement, submit daily:
31 20 00 - Page 2 of 6
Earth Moving


--- page 3 ---
1.   Field density reports per ASTM D6938 identifying test location, lift number, elevation, dry
density, moisture content, the ASTM D1557 Method C laboratory maximum dry density
and optimum moisture content used as denominators, percent compaction, and moisture
deviation from optimum.
1.6   SEQUENCING
A.   No structural fill shall be placed until the underlying subgrade has been proof-rolled in the
presence of the Laboratory and accepted in writing by the Owner's Representative Engineer.
B.   No fill placement shall proceed on any lift until the preceding lift has been tested and
accepted per Article 3.4.
PART 2    PRODUCTS
2.1   STRUCTURAL FILL
A.   Material. Well-graded granular fill classified SM or SW-SM, laboratory-tested per ASTM
D1557 Method C (modified Proctor) prior to placement.
B.   Gradation. Structural fill shall meet the following gradation, with no more than 12% passing
the No. 200 sieve and a plasticity index not exceeding 6.
C.   Deleterious Material. Structural fill shall be free of organic material, frozen soil, debris, and
particles greater than 3 inches in largest dimension.
D.   Laboratory Characterization. For each source and for each material change, the Laboratory
shall determine the maximum dry density and optimum moisture content by ASTM D1557
Method C prior to placement. The resulting laboratory values are the denominators against
which the acceptance criteria of Article 3.4.B are evaluated.
2.2   COMMON FILL
A.   Common fill placed outside the building envelope shall be free of organic material, debris, and
frozen soil, but is not subject to the acceptance criteria of Article 3.4.B.
2.3   CAPILLARY BREAK / DRAINAGE COURSE
A.   Clean, open-graded crushed stone, 3/4 in nominal, less than 2% passing the No. 200 sieve,
placed as shown on the Drawings beneath slabs-on-grade.
PART 3    EXECUTION
3.1   EXAMINATION
A.   Examine subgrade prior to fill placement. Do not proceed with fill placement over subgrade
that is soft, yielding under proof roll, frozen, or otherwise unsuitable. Notify the Owner's
Representative Engineer in writing of any unsuitable subgrade condition.
3.2   SUBGRADE PREPARATION
A.   Strip topsoil, organic material, and any existing uncontrolled fill from beneath the footprint of
structural fill.
B.   Proof-roll exposed subgrade with a loaded tandem-axle dump truck or equivalent equipment
approved in writing by the Owner's Representative Engineer. The Laboratory shall be present
31 20 00 - Page 3 of 6
Earth Moving


--- page 4 ---
to witness the proof roll.
C.   Undercut and replace yielding areas with structural fill placed and compacted per this
Section.
3.3   PLACEMENT
A.   Place structural fill in horizontal lifts not exceeding 12 inches loose thickness.
B.   Moisture-condition each lift, by wetting or drying and mixing, so that the moisture content at
the time of compaction is within the range specified in Article 3.4.B.
C.   Compact each lift with equipment sized and operated to achieve the density and moisture
requirements of Article 3.4.B throughout the full thickness of the lift.
D.   Do not place fill on frozen subgrade or with frozen material. Do not place fill during
precipitation that raises the placed material's moisture content above the upper limit of Article
3.4.B.
3.4   COMPACTION
A.   Method Statement. The Contractor shall place structural fill in controlled lifts as specified in
Article 3.3, moisture-conditioning each lift as necessary to bring the material within the
moisture range required by Article 3.4.B before compaction. Compaction equipment
(self-propelled vibratory smooth-drum rollers, pad-foot rollers, or plate compactors adjacent to
structures) shall be operated in a pattern of overlapping passes such that every location
within a lift receives no fewer than the number of passes established during a
Contractor-conducted test strip witnessed by the Laboratory and the Owner's Representative
Engineer. The test strip shall be executed at the start of production placement, using the
placement source, moisture-conditioning method, lift thickness, and compaction equipment
intended for production, and shall demonstrate that the criteria of Article 3.4.B are met before
general production is authorized. Adjacent to walls, columns, and utilities, use hand-operated
compaction equipment in lifts not exceeding 6 inches loose thickness. Do not operate heavy
compaction equipment within 3 feet of walls prior to backfill balancing on both sides. Each lift
shall be tested and accepted per Article 3.4.B before the next lift is placed.
B.   Acceptance Criteria.
Structural fill shall be placed and compacted to a dry density of not less than
95% of the maximum dry density determined by ASTM D1557 Method C for the
placed material, AND shall be placed at a moisture content within −1% to +2%
of the optimum moisture content determined by the same test. Both criteria must
be satisfied for each test location. Field density shall be measured per ASTM
D6938 (nuclear gauge, direct-transmission mode) at a frequency of one test per
5,000 sf per lift.
C.   Failing Tests. Where either the density criterion or the moisture criterion of Article 3.4.B is
not satisfied at any test location:
1.   The affected area of the lift shall be reworked (scarified, moisture-conditioned, and
recompacted, or removed and replaced) at the Contractor's expense.
2.   Reworked areas shall be retested by the Laboratory. Both the density and moisture
criteria of Article 3.4.B must be satisfied on the retest before the lift is accepted.
31 20 00 - Page 4 of 6
Earth Moving


--- page 5 ---
3.   Isolated failing tests may not be averaged with adjacent passing tests to demonstrate
compliance. Acceptance is evaluated at each test location independently.
D.   Interpretation. No test location shall be accepted on the basis of density alone. No test
location shall be accepted on the basis of moisture alone. Compliance requires that both the
density criterion and the moisture criterion of Article 3.4.B be independently satisfied at that
test location, as measured against the ASTM D1557 Method C laboratory maximum dry
density and optimum moisture content of the material actually placed at that location.
3.5   BACKFILL AGAINST FOUNDATION WALLS
A.   Do not commence backfill against basement or foundation walls until the wall has attained its
specified 28-day compressive strength, or until permanent lateral support (floor framing) is in
place and grouted to the wall, whichever occurs first.
B.   Place backfill on both sides of interior walls in balanced lifts not exceeding 12 inches loose
thickness, differing by no more than one lift side-to-side.
C.   Compact backfill to the same acceptance criteria as Article 3.4.B where the backfill supports
structure or slabs; elsewhere, to 90% of ASTM D1557 Method C maximum dry density.
3.6   SETTLEMENT TOLERANCE
A.   Total and Differential Settlement. Total settlement 1.0 in maximum; differential settlement
0.5 in maximum over 30 ft.
B.   Application. The tolerances of Paragraph A apply to the completed foundation system as
constructed on the accepted subgrade and structural fill delivered under this Section. Where
predicted or monitored settlements exceed the tolerances of Paragraph A, the Structural
Engineer of Record shall be notified in writing and no additional load shall be applied until a
written disposition is issued.
C.   Monitoring. Where settlement monitoring points are shown on the Drawings, readings shall
be taken and transmitted to the Owner's Representative Engineer at the frequency indicated.
Cumulative settlement approaching either tolerance of Paragraph A shall be reported
immediately.
3.7   FIELD QUALITY CONTROL
A.   Testing frequency for structural fill:
1.   In-place density and moisture: one ASTM D6938 test per 5,000 sf per lift, as required by
Article 3.4.B, and not fewer than three tests per lift regardless of lift area.
2.   Laboratory maximum dry density and optimum moisture content: one ASTM D1557
Method C determination per source, and one additional determination for each material
change identified by visual classification or gradation.
B.   Reporting. The Laboratory shall issue field density reports within 24 hours of testing. Each
report shall identify, for each test location, the ASTM D1557 Method C laboratory maximum
dry density and optimum moisture content used as the denominators, the measured dry
density, the measured moisture content, the percent compaction, the moisture deviation from
optimum, and the disposition (accept or reject) against Article 3.4.B.
C.   Non-Conforming Work. Any lift not meeting Article 3.4.B, or any lift for which the ASTM
D1557 Method C denominators used in reporting do not correspond to the material actually
placed, shall be reworked as required by Article 3.4.C before any additional lift is placed.

1. PURPOSE AND SCOPE
This memorandum establishes the governing codes, reference standards, site parameters, design loads, load
combinations, and serviceability criteria adopted for the structural design of Package A of the Birchwood Village
Expansion. Package A comprises three student-housing blocks (Blocks A, B and C) constructed over a shared
podium, one basement level beneath Blocks A and B, and a separate deep plant-room excavation planned beneath
Block B. The design basis stated herein governs all Package A calculations, drawings, and specifications issued
by the Engineer of Record and controls the interpretation of subordinate design documents where a conflict
arises.
This Rev.2 issue supersedes Rev.1 dated 07/18/2025. Substantive changes since Rev.1 are recorded in the
Revision Block on the final page.
2. GOVERNING CODES AND REFERENCE STANDARDS
The Project is designed in accordance with the following:
• Ohio Building Code (2024 edition, adopting IBC 2021 with Ohio amendments) — governing building
code as adopted by the State of Ohio; Chapter 16 (Structural Design) references ASCE 7-16 for loads.
• ACI 318-19, Building Code Requirements for Structural Concrete and Commentary — reinforced concrete
design, detailing, cover, and serviceability.
• ASCE 7-16, Minimum Design Loads and Associated Criteria for Buildings and Other Structures — dead,
live, snow, wind, seismic loads and load combinations.
• AISC 360-16, Specification for Structural Steel Buildings — structural steel members and connections at
podium framing and roof.
• ACI 301-20 for cast-in-place concrete construction requirements referenced through Spec 03 30 00.
• ASCE 32-01 for frost-protected shallow foundations where applicable at Block C perimeter.
Materials and test methods are governed by the specifications listed in Section 03 20 00, 03 30 00, and 31 20 00
(Rev.2, current at the date of this memorandum), and where cited by ASTM designation on the drawings.
Where an inconsistency arises between the Ohio Building Code (adopting IBC 2021) and a referenced consensus
standard, the more stringent provision governs unless the Ohio amendment expressly modifies the standard.

6. LOAD COMBINATIONS
Strength design (LRFD) load combinations for gravity, wind, and seismic follow ASCE 7-16 §2.3.1. Allowable
stress combinations (ASD) per §2.4 are used only for soil-structure interaction checks at the geotechnical
interface (bearing pressure, settlement) and are stated in the geotechnical calculation package. Load combinations
relevant to Package A are set out in full below.
6.1 Basic Strength Load Combinations — ASCE 7-16 §2.3.1
(1)  1.4D
(2)  1.2D + 1.6L + 0.5(Lr or S or R)
(3)  1.2D + 1.6(Lr or S or R) + (L or 0.5W)
(4)  1.2D + 1.0W + L + 0.5(Lr or S or R)
(5)  1.2D + Ev + Eh + L + 0.2S
(6)  0.9D + 1.0W
(7)  0.9D − Ev + Eh
Where:
D = dead load; L = live load; Lr = roof live; S = snow; R = rain; W = wind; E = earthquake with vertical Ev =
0.2·SDS·D and horizontal Eh = ρ·QE component.
6.2 Counteracting Combinations — ASCE 7-16 §2.3.1(6)–(7)
Combinations (6) and (7) — 0.9D + W and 0.9D − E + E — apply where the dead load counteracts (rather than
compounds) the effect of the variable load. 
This governs:
• Flotation and uplift. A permanent load that resists overturning, sliding, uplift or flotation
is taken at 0.9D, with an explicit factor of safety stated; minimum 1.5 for sliding and base heave.
• Overturning of shear walls. Wind and seismic overturning at Blocks A, B and C shear walls, and at
podium transfer walls, are checked with 0.9D on the resisting side.
• Uplift on Block B piles under wind and seismic. Piles are checked for reversal per §12.13 with 0.9D on
the gravity leg.

A23=Scope
A24=Vantree Materials Testing, LLC ("Vantree" or "the Laboratory") was contracted to the Owner, Thornbury State University, to perform geotechnical laboratory index testing on samples recovered by Kelbrook Geotechnical, Inc. from Borings B-01 through B-09 drilled at the Package A site during the field exploration period 10/28/2024 through 11/22/2024. Samples were received under chain-of-custody on 11/25/2024, logged in as project VMT-2024-0917-PkgA-INDEX, and stored at the Laboratory's climate-controlled sample room until testing. The results are presented in the INDEX TESTS sheet, with Package A design unit weights compiled in the SUMMARY sheet.
A26=ASTM test methods
A27=The following ASTM standards apply to the tests reported in this workbook:
A29=Method	B29=Title
A30=ASTM D422	B30=Standard Test Method for Particle-Size Analysis of Soils (grain-size distribution; sieve and hydrometer)
A31=ASTM D4318	B31=Standard Test Methods for Liquid Limit, Plastic Limit, and Plasticity Index of Soils (Atterberg limits)
A32=ASTM D2216	B32=Standard Test Methods for Laboratory Determination of Water (Moisture) Content of Soil and Rock by Mass
A33=ASTM D854	B33=Standard Test Methods for Specific Gravity of Soil Solids by Water Pycnometer
A34=ASTM D7263	B34=Standard Test Methods for Laboratory Determination of Density (Unit Weight) of Soil Specimens
A35=ASTM D2487	B35=Standard Practice for Classification of Soils for Engineering Purposes (Unified Soil Classification System) — used to assign USCS group symbols
A37=Grain-size distributions in the INDEX TESTS sheet were determined in accordance with ASTM D422. Atterberg limits (LL, PL, PI) were determined in accordance with ASTM D4318, Method A (multipoint liquid-limit method) for the cohesive samples; the granular SP-SM and SW-GW samples are non-plastic (NP) as determined by the plastic-limit test in accordance with ASTM D4318. Natural moisture contents were determined on the recovered field mass in accordance with ASTM D2216. Specific gravity of solids was determined on representative fines in accordance with ASTM D854. Total (moist) unit weight was determined on trimmed sub-specimens of the thin-walled Shelby-tube samples in accordance with ASTM D7263.
A39=Sample inventory
A40=Samples tested comprise (a) recovered split-spoon (SPT) sub-samples from all nine borings for classification, moisture and grain-size analysis, and (b) thin-walled Shelby-tube (undisturbed) sub-specimens from the clay aquitard for unit-weight determination. The Shelby-tube samples designated B-04 U-1, B-06 U-1, B-06 U-2, B-06 U3, B-08 U-1, and B-08 U2 were received. Of these, B-06 U3 and B-08 U2 were also forwarded to the Laboratory's consolidation test bench for ASTM D2435 one-dimensional consolidation testing; the D2435 results are reported separately in workbook Consolidation_Test_Data_D2435.xlsx (Vantree Laboratory Report No. VMT-2025-0109-CON). Trimmings from B-06 U3 and B-08 U2 were retained for the index tests reported herein so that the soil classification and Atterberg limits are common between the two reports. Natural moisture content and density were determined independently on each test bench, on separate trimmings taken at different levels within the tube, and are reported as measured by each; the unit weights tabulated herein are the values furnished for design use in the stratum.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Independent verification of Item 051 — Block C spread-footing long-term settlement.
All inputs are read from the project record; every result is printed with its source.
Run: python3 /tmp/ahpele/verify.py
"""
import math, os, statistics
import openpyxl

ROOT = "/filesystem/Birchwood/PackageA"
GAMMA_W = 62.4  # pcf

def val(ws, cell):
    return ws[cell].value

def num(ws, cell):
    v = ws[cell].value
    if isinstance(v, (int, float)):
        return float(v)
    import re
    m = re.search(r"[-+]?\d[\d,]*(?:\.\d+)?", str(v))
    if not m:
        raise ValueError(f"no number in {ws.title}!{cell}: {v!r}")
    return float(m.group(0).replace(",", ""))

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- source inputs
cb = openpyxl.load_workbook(os.path.join(ROOT, "02_Structural/Calcs/CB-GEO-007_Settlement_BlockC.xlsx"), data_only=True)
cover = cb["Cover"]; s2 = cb["Sheet 2 INPUT"]; s3 = cb["Sheet 3 Schmertmann"]; s4 = cb["Sheet 4 Consolidation"]
crit_total = num(cover, "B23")          # 1.0 in
crit_diff = num(cover, "B24")           # 0.5 in
crit_ang = str(val(cover, "B25"))              # 1/500
footing_bottom = num(s2, "F6")           # El. 740.5
H = num(s2, "F9")                        # 18 ft
sigma0_design = num(s2, "F11")           # 1,850 psf
dsigma = num(s2, "F12")                  # 900 psf
immediate_max = num(s3, "G50")           # 0.9 in
immediate_min = num(s3, "G51")           # 0.7 in
immediate_F6 = num(s3, "G43")            # 0.90 in, F-C6
immediate_F7 = num(s3, "G44")            # 0.82 in, F-C7
diff_immediate = num(s3, "E61")          # 0.2 in
sheet4_note = str(val(s4, "A15"))

# Consolidation parameters (Vantree VMT-2025-0109-CON Summary)
con = openpyxl.load_workbook(os.path.join(ROOT, "01_Geotech/Consolidation_Test_Data_D2435.xlsx"), data_only=True)
summ = con["Summary — Design Params"]
Cc = num(summ, "B11"); Cr = num(summ, "B12"); e0 = num(summ, "B13")
sigma0_lab = num(summ, "B14"); sigmap = num(summ, "B15"); H_lab = num(summ, "B16")
cv_cm2s = 4.4e-4
cv_ft2day = cv_cm2s * 0.0001 / 0.3048**2 * 86400  # cm2/s -> ft2/day
Hdr = H / 2.0

# Monitoring (Settlement_Monitoring_BlockC.xlsx)
mon = openpyxl.load_workbook(os.path.join(ROOT, "05_Field/Settlement_Monitoring_BlockC.xlsx"), data_only=True)
rd = mon["Readings"]
header = [c.value for c in rd[4]]
mp_cols = {h: i for i, h in enumerate(header) if isinstance(h, str) and h.startswith("MP-")}
rounds = []
for row in rd.iter_rows(min_row=5, values_only=True):
    if row[0] is None or not isinstance(row[0], (int, float)):
        continue
    rounds.append(row)
last = rounds[-1]
first = rounds[0]
mp_last = {mp: float(last[i]) for mp, i in mp_cols.items()}
mp_first = {mp: float(first[i]) for mp, i in mp_cols.items()}
max_mp = min(mp_last, key=mp_last.get)
max_sett = -mp_last[max_mp]
min_mp = max(mp_last, key=mp_last.get)
min_sett = -mp_last[min_mp]
range_sett = max_sett - min_sett
# Adjacent-pair differential within a 30-ft gauge (grid 24 ft x 26 ft; diagonal 35.4 ft > 30 ft)
coords = {
    "MP-1": (0,0), "MP-2": (1,0), "MP-3": (2,0), "MP-4": (3,0),
    "MP-5": (0,1), "MP-6": (1,1), "MP-7": (2,1), "MP-8": (3,1),
    "MP-9": (0,2), "MP-10": (1,2), "MP-11": (2,2), "MP-12": (3,2),
}
max_adj, max_adj_pair = 0.0, None
for a in mp_last:
    for b in mp_last:
        if a >= b:
            continue
        dx = (coords[a][0]-coords[b][0])*24.0
        dy = (coords[a][1]-coords[b][1])*26.0
        dist = math.hypot(dx, dy)
        if dist <= 30.0:
            diff = abs(mp_last[a]-mp_last[b])
            if diff > max_adj:
                max_adj, max_adj_pair = diff, (a, b, dist)
mp7_col = mp_cols["MP-7"]
mp7_series = [float(r[mp7_col]) for r in rounds]
mp7_inc = [mp7_series[i]-mp7_series[i-1] for i in range(1, len(mp7_series))]
first3_rate = -sum(mp7_inc[:3])/42.0
last3_rate = -sum(mp7_inc[-3:])/42.0
last_rate = -mp7_inc[-1]/14.0
days = 196  # 12/12/2025 to 06/26/2026

# profile-derived effective stress at mid-clay (El. 729), GIR Table 6-1
sigma_v = 12.0*118.0 + 9.0*120.0  # 12 ft sand + 9 ft clay to mid-layer
u = (742.0-729.0)*GAMMA_W
sigma0_profile = sigma_v - u

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- calculations
def sc_nc(sigma0, dsigma, cc=Cc, h=H, e=e0):
    return cc*h/(1.0+e)*math.log10((sigma0+dsigma)/sigma0)

def sc_oc(sigma0, dsigma, sigp=sigmap, cr=Cr, cc=Cc, h=H, e=e0):
    sf = sigma0 + dsigma
    if sf <= sigp:
        return cr*h/(1.0+e)*math.log10(sf/sigma0)
    return (cr*h/(1.0+e)*math.log10(sigp/sigma0)
            + cc*h/(1.0+e)*math.log10(sf/sigp))

sc_design_ft = sc_nc(sigma0_design, dsigma)
sc_design_in = sc_design_ft*12.0
sc_profile_in = sc_nc(sigma0_profile, dsigma)*12.0
sc_oc_in = sc_oc(sigma0_design, dsigma)*12.0
total_design = immediate_max + sc_design_in
total_profile = immediate_max + sc_profile_in
util_total_design = total_design/crit_total
util_total_profile = total_profile/crit_total
util_cons_design = sc_design_in/crit_total
util_diff_measured = range_sett/crit_diff
util_ang_immediate = (1.0/2150.0)/(1.0/500.0)
t90_days = 0.848*Hdr**2/cv_ft2day
t50_days = 0.197*Hdr**2/cv_ft2day
Tv_now = cv_ft2day*days/Hdr**2
U_now = math.sqrt(4*Tv_now/math.pi)/(1+(4*Tv_now/math.pi)**2.8)**0.179
days_to_tol_last = (crit_total-max_sett)/last_rate
days_to_tol_avg3 = (crit_total-max_sett)/last3_rate

print("ITEM 051 — INDEPENDENT RECOMPUTATION")
print("="*72)
print("Inputs (source):")
print(f"  Clay layer H                 = {H:.1f} ft  (CB-GEO-007 Sheet 2 F9; GIR Rev.2 Table 6-1)")
print(f"  Cc, Cr, e0                   = {Cc:.3f}, {Cr:.3f}, {e0:.2f}  (VMT-2025-0109-CON Summary)")
print(f"  sigma'0 design / lab         = {sigma0_design:,.0f} psf  (CB-GEO-007 F11; VMT Summary B14)")
print(f"  sigma'p                      = {sigmap:,.0f} psf  (VMT Summary B15)")
print(f"  Delta sigma at mid-clay      = {dsigma:,.0f} psf  (CB-GEO-007 F12; Item 051)")
print(f"  Immediate settlement max     = {immediate_max:.2f} in  (CB-GEO-007 Sheet 3 G50)")
print(f"  CB-GEO-007 Sheet 4 note      = {sheet4_note!r}")
print(f"  Design tolerance total/diff  = {crit_total:.2f} in / {crit_diff:.2f} in over 30 ft  (Spec 31 20 00 Rev.3 Art. 3.6.A)")
print()
print("Effective stress check at El. 729.0:")
print(f"  sigma_v = 12*118 + 9*120       = {sigma_v:,.1f} psf")
print(f"  u       = (742.0-729.0)*62.4   = {u:,.1f} psf")
print(f"  sigma'0 = sigma_v - u          = {sigma0_profile:,.1f} psf  (vs {sigma0_design:,.0f} psf stated)")
print()
print("Consolidation settlement, Sc = Cc*H/(1+e0)*log10((sigma'0+dsigma)/sigma'0):")
print(f"  using sigma'0 = {sigma0_design:,.0f} psf (report basis): {sc_design_in:.2f} in")
print(f"  using sigma'0 = {sigma0_profile:,.0f} psf (profile):     {sc_profile_in:.2f} in")
print(f"  OC check (Cr to sigma'p, Cc above):                     {sc_oc_in:.2f} in")
print()
print("Total settlement (immediate + primary consolidation):")
print(f"  report basis: {immediate_max:.2f} + {sc_design_in:.2f} = {total_design:.2f} in  vs {crit_total:.2f} in -> utilisation {util_total_design:.2f}")
print(f"  profile basis:{immediate_max:.2f} + {sc_profile_in:.2f} = {total_profile:.2f} in  vs {crit_total:.2f} in -> utilisation {util_total_profile:.2f}")
print(f"  consolidation alone / tolerance: {sc_design_in:.2f}/{crit_total:.2f} = {util_cons_design:.2f}")
print()
print("Monitoring (12/12/2025 to 06/26/2026, 15 rounds, 196 days):")
print(f"  maximum settlement  = {max_sett:.2f} in at {max_mp}")
print(f"  minimum settlement  = {min_sett:.2f} in at {min_mp}")
print(f"  measured range      = {range_sett:.2f} in  (overall MP-7 to MP-12)")
print(f"  max adjacent pair within 30 ft = {max_adj:.2f} in at {max_adj_pair[0]}-{max_adj_pair[1]} ({max_adj_pair[2]:.1f} ft), {max_adj/crit_diff*100:.0f}% of {crit_diff:.2f} in differential tolerance")
